item.content:encoded: Die Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) steht einem Medienbericht zufolge vor dem Einstieg bei der portugiesischen Fluggesellschaft TAP. Der deutsche Konzern werde den Zuschlag für einen Anteil von 44,9 Prozent erhalten und sich damit gegen den Rivalen Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) durchsetzen, berichtete der Fernsehsender SIC am Dienstagabend unter Berufung auf Insider. Die Lufthansa biete den Kaufpreis vollständig in bar an, während die Offerte des französisch-niederländischen Konkurrenten eine Mischung aus Bargeld und Aktien vorsehe. Zudem habe die stärkere Finanzlage der Deutschen den Ausschlag gegeben. Das portugiesische Infrastrukturministerium lehnte eine Stellungnahme ab. Die Regierung will am Mittwoch auf einer außerordentlichen Kabinettssitzung über den Gewinner entscheiden. Air France-KLM und die Lufthansa hatten im September ihre endgültigen Gebote für die Beteiligung eingereicht. Zuvor hatte die portugiesische Regierung beide Interessenten [USN:L8N44W13X TEXT:"um Nachbesserungen gebeten"].

item.content:encoded: Das Hamburger Biotech-Unternehmen Evotec (EVTG.DE) hat sich nach eigenen Angaben in den ersten neun Monaten des laufenden Jahres besser entwickelt als erwartet. Auf Basis vorläufiger Ergebnisse werde für den Zeitraum ein Konzernumsatz von rund 465 Millionen Euro und ein bereinigter Konzern-Verlust (Ebitda) von rund 42,8 Millionen Euro erwartet, [USN:EQ3YWRWda TEXT:"teilte das im SDax notierte Unternehmen"] am Dienstagabend mit. "Diese Zahlen liegen über den aktuellen Markterwartungen, wobei die Abweichung im Wesentlichen auf die zeitliche Verteilung der Konsensschätzungen zurückzuführen ist", hieß es. Für das Gesamtjahr 2026 bestätigte Evotec die Prognose eines Konzernumsatzes zwischen 570 und 610 Millionen Euro (595 bis 635 Millionen bei konstanten Wechselkursen) und eines bereinigten Konzern-EBITDA von rund minus 70 bis minus 105 Millionen Euro (minus 60 bis minus 90 Millionen Euro bei konstanten Wechselkursen). Mitte Juli hatte Evotec [USN:L8N43G0FT TEXT:"seine Jahresziele drastisch gesenkt"]. Als Hauptgründe waren verzögerte Meilensteinzahlungen und später als geplante Abschlüsse neuer Partnerschaften genannt worden.

item.title: India's Bank of Baroda says it will defend interests after UAE businessman Shetty files $15 bln suit
item.description: India's Bank of Baroda on Wednesday said it will protect its interests, a day after UAE-based businessman and founder of NMC Health filed a $15 billion case against the lender and 25 other defendants in the Bombay High Court.
item.dc:creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Gopika Gopakumar
item.content:encoded: India's Bank of Baroda (BOB.NS) on Wednesday said it will protect its interests, a day after UAE-based businessman and founder of NMC Health filed a $15 billion case against the lender and 25 other defendants in the Bombay High Court. NMC Health founder B.R. Shetty alleged that Bank of Baroda and several current and former employees helped facilitate a fraud that contributed to the collapse of the Middle East healthcare group, according to a court filing reviewed by Reuters. The firm, then the Gulf's largest private healthcare provider, was [USN:L8N2EH32C TEXT:"placed under administration"] in 2020 after months of financial mismanagement, and disclosed debts of $6.6 billion, above earlier estimates of $2.1 billion. Representatives for Shetty did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. In a stock exchange notification on Wednesday, the country's second-largest state lender said, "The Bank has not been served with such a suit and cannot comment on the contents of pleadings which are untested in court. If and when the Bank is served, the Bank will defend the suit firmly and take all steps necessary to protect its interests." Bank of Baroda added that it was pursuing recovery and enforcement proceedings in India and UAE against Shetty for outstanding dues of 28 billion rupees ($294.57 million) and had obtained several decrees against him. The lender will not bear any immediate liability till any order is passed and/or till it is required to make a provision on account of potential damages, the lender said. Bank of Baroda shares dropped 2.6% on Tuesday after the suit was reported. The stock is down 2.6% at 231.4 rupees on Wednesday. The lawsuit, which centres on the bank's lending to NMC Health and affiliated entities in the UAE, comes three months after the lender agreed to pay $600 million to settle claims brought by administrators of NMC. Shetty alleged that bank officials enabled round-tripping transactions, ignored repeated anti-money laundering warnings and accepted documents bearing forged signatures. He is seeking $5 billion in direct damages, $5 billion in consequential damages and an additional $5 billion for reputational harm, the filing showed. ($1 = 95.0525 Indian rupees)

item.title: Renshaw's heroics do little to solve Australia's opening puzzle
item.description: Matt Renshaw's match-winning heroics against South Africa have given Australia another strong middle-order option but done little to resolve the uncertainty over their opening combination ahead of the second test in Gqeberha.
item.dc:creator: Ian Ransom
item.content:encoded: Matt Renshaw's match-winning heroics against South Africa have given Australia another strong middle-order option but done little to resolve the uncertainty over their opening combination ahead of the second test in Gqeberha. With Renshaw producing a majestic 190 and second-innings 82 batting at number five in the [USN:L6N45Z0QL TEXT:"commanding 214-run victory"] in Durban, the Queenslander's shift down the order looks to have been a masterstroke. Captain Pat Cummins said it would take a compelling argument to shift Renshaw again for Sunday's second test, though he was enthusiastic about the options available. "I still think he can be a great opener, and now he's got another string to his bow that he's found this week," Cummins said. Coming nearly 10 years after his first test century against Pakistan, 30-year-old Renshaw's second ton was a reward for perseverance for a player dropped repeatedly since his 2016 debut. His breakthrough has not settled the lingering questions over the team's opening batters, however. Travis Head, who had great success as a middle-order blaster, has continued at the top of the order after a brilliant Ashes as a stand-in opener, but doubts remain over his suitability for the role. After a lean home series against Bangladesh, Head managed a total of 20 runs in Durban operating with Nic Maddinson, the latest to emerge through Australia's revolving door of selections. "Travis Head's done a very good job as an opener, but my gut feel is that he's better off in the middle order," said former Australia captain Allan Border. Supported by a handy lead, 34-year-old Maddinson smashed 48 from 38 balls in his second innings after an ugly, 33-ball duck under greater pressure in the first innings. The possible return of Cameron Green from an abdominal strain could further complicate Australia's selection decisions, though the all-rounder would be restricted to batting duties if cleared to play. While it was the rejuvenated Renshaw setting the platform for victory, it was Australia's time-worn attack delivering the knockout blow, led by Josh Hazlewood's career-best 6-49 in the fourth innings. Like Mitchell Starc before him, Hazlewood has made a hugely impressive comeback from a difficult period of injuries, helping to keep an ageing team at the top of test cricket. Coach Andrew McDonald has said changes are inevitable as the team progresses through a gruelling schedule of 20 tests through next year's Ashes, or 21 if they reach the World Test Championship final at The Oval in June. Cummins suggested none of his bowlers would be putting their hands up for a rest. "One thing I’ve always loved about Joshy and Starcy is they’re just so happy getting into the grind. They’ll never shy away from having a bowl," he said.

item.title: ASML forecasts Q4 sales above expectations on AI chip demand
item.description: ASML on Wednesday forecast fourth-quarter sales above analyst expectations, as AI-driven demand for its chipmaking equipment remains strong, and narrowed its 2026 outlook.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ASML (ASML.AS) on Wednesday forecast fourth-quarter sales above analyst expectations, as AI-driven demand for its chipmaking equipment remains strong, and narrowed its 2026 outlook. The Dutch company guided for fourth-quarter net sales of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion ($15.9 billion to $17.0 billion) and a gross margin of around 57%. Analysts polled by LSEG had expected sales of €14.19 billion and a gross margin of 55.4%. It narrowed the 2026 net sales outlook to between €44 billion and €45 billion, having previously seen a range of €43 billion to €45 billion, with a gross margin of around 56%. ASML, the world's largest supplier of chipmaking equipment and the only maker of the EUV machines needed for the most advanced chips, is a bellwether for the AI buildout. ($1 = 0.8924 euros)

item.title: How European stocks can weather higher energy prices
item.description: The latest rise in oil and gas prices has renewed concerns about Europe's reliance on imported fuel and its potential impact on companies as winter approaches.
item.dc:creator: Danilo Masoni
item.content:encoded: The latest rise in [USN:L1N45201P TEXT:"oil"] and [USN:L6N45Z0ID TEXT:"gas"] prices has renewed concerns about Europe's reliance on imported fuel and its potential impact on companies as winter approaches. Portfolio managers, however, say European listed companies overall are in a markedly different position than in 2022, when soaring gas prices in the wake of Russia's invasion of Ukraine sparked recession fears and competitiveness concerns. ENERGY'S LOW SHARE IN TOTAL COSTS "When we look at the big listed companies in Europe, the upfront hit is quite manageable," said Ciaran Callaghan, head of European equity research at Amundi. "It's more consumers who are taking the hit, and maybe some smaller companies ... that probably don't have as diversified energy sources." While chemicals, materials and airline sectors remain exposed, Morgan Stanley estimates direct energy costs are only a low single-digit share of costs for many industrial companies. Deutsche Bank estimates energy costs make up 1% of sales for STOXX 600 (.STOXX) companies overall. INDEX MIX HELPS Sectors that benefit from higher energy prices account for 36% of MSCI Europe (.dMIEU00000PUS) earnings, compared with about 6% generated by sectors at risk, according to Morgan Stanley. Among the beneficiaries are energy, utilities and banks and those sectors' share of index market capitalisation has risen to 25% from 16% five years ago. Thomas O'Hara, investment director for European equities at GAM Investments, said European indexes are less vulnerable than in the past because of both their changed composition and companies' greater experience in handling energy-driven inflation. "This is a market and a real economy that is more experienced in dealing with the challenges of inflation catalysed by higher energy costs," he said. Energy-intensive sectors such as chemicals, steel and autos now account for a smaller share of European indexes, he noted, while banks, which benefit from higher interest rates that typically accompany spells of elevated inflation, represent a much larger weighting. AI BOOM BOOSTS EARNINGS Amundi's Callaghan said spending linked to artificial intelligence was also providing support for industrial and technology suppliers, more than compensating for the energy shock. "There is a massive AI boom and that's feeding its way into the European market," he said. Direct beneficiaries of AI-related capital spending account for 8% of MSCI Europe earnings. GLOBAL PRESENCE HELPS "European listed companies are not a proxy for their domestic economies," said Gilles Guibout, head of European equities at BNP Paribas Asset Management. "They are global." Many firms now manufacture closer to their end-markets while generating a large share of revenue outside Europe, reducing exposure to regional costs and supply disruptions. Europe accounts for 42% of STOXX 600 members' revenues, according to Goldman Sachs. COMPANIES ADAPTED GAM's O'Hara said companies have spent the past four years strengthening supply chains, improving procurement contracts and learning how to manage inflation shocks. Europe has also increased LNG imports, developed alternative supply routes and increased use of hedging, renewables and energy-efficiency measures. "In 2022, firms were reacting to an energy shock. Today, energy risk management is a structural part of how they run their business," Mario Montagnani, senior investment strategist at Vontobel, said. Since the Iran war started in February, all sectors, besides consumer ones, have seen earnings upgrades, according to Goldman Sachs. RISKS REMAIN Anthony Penel, European equities manager at Edmond de Rothschild Asset Management, however, sees limits to European companies' resilience and views markets as too complacent. "They can't do miracles," he said, warning that if high oil and gas prices persist into 2027, the damage would show up indirectly through inflation, higher borrowing costs and weaker demand.

item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: Papst Leo ist an Lungenkrebs erkrankt. Dem 71-Jährigen sei bei einer Operation am Dienstag der untere rechte Lungenlappen entfernt worden, teilte der Vatikan am Abend mit. Dabei habe eine Gewebeuntersuchung den Verdacht auf ein sogenanntes Adenokarzinom bestätigt, eine häufige Form von Lungenkrebs. Der Eingriff in der Gemelli-Klinik in Rom sei aber erfolgreich verlaufen. Der Pontifex sei normal aufgewacht und erhole sich in seinem Krankenzimmer. Die Diagnose kann gleichwohl einen erheblichen gesundheitlichen Rückschlag für den Papst bedeuten. Eine Prognose dazu gab es am Dienstag zunächst aber nicht. Der leitende Chirurg des Papstes, Dr. Stefano Margaritora, und sein Leibarzt, Dr. Luigi Carbone, erklärten in einer Stellungnahme, dass der Eingriff etwa 90 Minuten dauerte und erfolgreich verlief, ohne dass Komplikationen auftraten. "Um den Eingriff kurativ zu gestalten, wurde der Unterlappen der rechten Lunge mithilfe einer videoassistierten Technik entfernt", erklärten sie und machten damit deutlich, dass das Ziel darin bestand, das gesamte Krebsgewebe zu entfernen. Gewebeproben, die während der Operation entnommen wurden, hätten den Verdacht der Ärzte bestätigt, der bereits bei vorbereitenden Untersuchungen aufgekommen war, hieß es. Außenstehende Mediziner erklärten, zur Beurteilung des Falls und der Prognose müsse man die Größe des entfernten Tumors sowie die Information kennen, ob sich der Krebs auf die Lymphknoten ausgebreitet habe. Dazu machte der Vatikan aber keine Angaben. "Wir kennen zwar die Diagnose, aber noch nicht das Stadium. Dies ist entscheidend für die Prognose und die Behandlung", sagte Stephen Liu, Lungenkrebsexperte an der Georgetown University in Washington und Abteilungsleiter für Hämatologie und Onkologie am MedStar Georgetown University Hospital. "Wenn es sich um einen kleinen Lungenkrebs ohne Befall der Lymphknoten handelt, dürfte die Operation allein bereits heilend wirken", sagte Liu der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. "Sollte die abschließende Analyse jedoch einen größeren Befall durch den Krebs ergeben, deutet dies auf eine schlechtere Prognose hin." Anfang der Woche hatte der Vatikan mitgeteilt, Leo werde voraussichtlich etwa eine Woche im Krankenhaus bleiben und alle seine öffentlichen Termine bis zum 20. Oktober seien abgesagt worden. Leo war im Mai 2025 zum Nachfolger des im Alter von 88 Jahren verstorbenen Papstes Franziskus gewählt worden. Er gilt für einen Kirchenführer als verhältnismäßig jung. Leo treibt Sport, spielt unter anderem Tennis und ist nicht als Raucher bekannt. Auch gesundheitliche Probleme gab es zuletzt nicht. Vom 6. bis zum 17. November ist eine Reise nach Uruguay, Argentinien und Peru geplant. Einen Stellvertreter für das Oberhaupt der weltweit 1,4 Milliarden Katholiken gibt es nicht. Im Falle einer Erkrankung des Papstes arbeitet die Verwaltung des Vatikans regulär weiter, Entscheidungen, die seine Zustimmung erfordern, werden aber aufgeschoben. Leo wurde 1955 als Robert Prevost in Chicago geboren und wirkte jahrzehntelang als Missionar und Bischof in Peru. Dort überlebte er 1985 als junger Priester eine schwere Typhus-Erkrankung.

item.title: Flames notch 1st win, continue success in road games against Ducks
item.description: Martin Pospisil broke a late third-period tie and the Calgary Flames won for the first time this season with a 4-2 victory over the host Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Martin Pospisil broke a late third-period tie and the Calgary Flames won for the first time this season with a 4-2 victory over the host Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday. Rookie Aydar Suniev collected one goal and one assist to post his first career multi-point effort in his 10th career game over parts of three seasons. Adam Klapka and Yegor Sharangovich both tallied once for the Flames, who lost their first five games of the campaign. Goaltender Dustin Wolf made 23 saves. Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson replied for the Ducks, who received a 32-save performance from goalie Lukas Dostal. With overtime looming, Pospisil zoomed up the ice, faked a shot until he moved to the right faceoff dot and whipped a low shot into the cage with 4:22 remaining. Sharangovich added an empty-net goal three minutes later to round out the scoring. The Flames have won 58 consecutive games when they score four or more goals. They have won 11 of the last 13 visits to Anaheim (11-0-2). Calgary may sit at the bottom of the league standings, but played better after losing to the visiting Ducks 4-2 on Saturday. The Flames had the early edge in play on Tuesday and were rewarded when Klapka opened the scoring at 8:32 with a seeing-eye shot from the high slot. Anaheim responded with a pair to take the lead. Sennecke put the hosts on the board at 12:09 when he stole a puck at his blue line, sprung himself for a breakaway and converted a high shot during 4-on-4 play. Carlsson then put Anaheim ahead with a power-play goal two minutes later when he buried a top-shelf shot from the right faceoff dot. With his assist on Carlsson's goal, Mikael Granlund became the first player in franchise history to start a season with a six-game point streak. Suniev pulled Calgary even with his second goal in as many games when he found the mark with a one-timer from the slot at 8:02. The goal came seconds after Calgary failed to convert during a full two-minute 5-on-3 advantage. With forwards Cutter Gauthier and Ryan Poehling sidelined due to injuries suffered in the first half of the home-and-home series with Calgary, the Ducks summoned 2025 first-round draft pick Roger McQueen for his NHL debut. --Field Level Media

item.title: ACLS notebook: Freddy Peralta flourishing since trade from Mets to Rays
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays hadn't lost consecutive games in almost three weeks entering Game 2 of the American League Championship Series on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays hadn't lost consecutive games in almost three weeks entering Game 2 of the American League Championship Series on Tuesday. They still haven't. A key trade deadline acquisition had a massive part in it, as starter Freddy Peralta allowed just four hits and two walks with six strikeouts in six innings of a 3-1 victory over the visiting Cleveland Guardians. Acquired in an August deal with the New York Mets in exchange for three minor leaguers, Peralta threw 68 of 99 pitches for strikes. Middling with the Mets, Peralta, 30, continues to flourish in Tampa Bay. The right-hander posted 5-2 record with a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular-season starts with the Rays, including a September run when he went 4-0 with a 0.96 ERA and was named the AL Pitcher of the Month. Peralta followed that with a 4 2/3-inning, one-run effort in a Game 2 win over the New York Yankees in the American League Division Series. On Tuesday, he hit a season-high with a 99.4 mph fastball. "I define myself as a competitor, and I like these kinds of games," said Peralta, a two-time All-Star in his first eight MLB seasons with the Milwaukee Brewers. "I've always said it in the past, that I enjoy this. "As a Dominican pitcher, I grew up watching the games in New York, and that's the game that you see," he continued, "and I get used to that because I grew up watching it, and I feel that I have that in me, in myself, and that's the way that I feel when I'm on the mound in these kind of games." Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick entered the day with a 2-1 record and 1.03 ERA in four career starts against the Rays. The rookie allowed three unearned runs on six hits and two walks, with three strikeouts in five innings. The loss was his second of three postseason starts. BIG MISTAKE: In a series that has felt closer than the 5-1 regular-season advantage Tampa Bay held over Cleveland, a key fielding error by third baseman Jose Ramirez set up all three Rays runs in the fourth. That opportunism would be a welcome element for Rays manager Kevin Cash heading into Game 3 on Thursday in Cleveland. "Jose Ramirez is as good as any third baseman there is in the game," he said. "And we were fortunate to maybe catch a break there. But once you catch a break, it's kind of what you do with it." CONTAINMENT: Tampa Bay limited the Guardians to one run by holding their lineup core of Ramirez and Chase DeLauter relatively in check at 2-for-6 with an RBI collectively and shutting down Jo Adell, who had delivered a game-sealing two-run double in Cleveland's 7-3 victory in Game 1 on Monday. On Tuesday night, DeLauter walked after Ramirez had singled with two outs in the fifth and stolen second. However, Peralta induced a lineout from Adell to end the threat with Tampa Bay leading, 3-0. In the seventh, DeLauter delivered a two-out, run-scoring double after left-hander Ian Seymour had entered in a platoon match-up, but Adell struck out to snuff the rally. Adell finished 0-for-4. J-RAM: Still, Ramirez has reached base safely in 14 consecutive postseason games, tying him for second-longest such streak in Cleveland history. A 16-game run by teammate Steven Kwan from 2022-24 leads the club. Jim Thome managed a 14-game streak from 1996-98. Ramirez had recorded an RBI in four straight postseason games, which is tied with Jim Thome (Oct. 11, 1998 to Oct. 7, 1999) for the longest streak in Cleveland postseason history. Kwan and DeLauter have hit safely in six straight games, the longest active streaks in the 2026 postseason. RALLY-KILLER: Cleveland looked to have completed a third double play by the fourth inning when Victor Mesa Jr. bounced to second baseman Travis Bazzana, but Mesa Jr. was ruled safe at first after a Rays challenge. The Tropicana Field crowd was roaring for Mesa and Junior Caminero -- who had a leadoff walk -- to potentially be safe when video replays focused on shortstop Brayan Rocchio's pivot at second base. After a long delay, video officials ruled that he had made shoe contact with the base while taking in Bazzana's feed. The out call stood on Caminero at second, but Mesa was safe at first. "It looked like we didn't quite get a good exchange on that ball," Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. "We didn't quite get a good feed and quick turn. Any time your rhythm gets broken up on a double-play ball like that, it's going to be tough to really turn it. I thought we had a couple plays on defense that we normally convert things." That reversal became crucial, with speedy Chandler Simpson reaching on a high-chopped single with two outs and Ramirez allowing a Ben Williamson grounder through his legs for a 1-0 Rays lead. Liam Hicks then lashed a two-run single to give Tampa Bay a 3-0 edge after five innings. --Brant James, Field Level Media

item.title: PSG boss Luis Enrique hopes Man City are not stripped of titles
item.description: Paris St Germain boss Luis Enrique said Manchester City were deserving winners of their trophies and should be allowed to keep them, despite the English club facing sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Paris St Germain boss Luis Enrique said Manchester City were deserving winners of their trophies and should be allowed to keep them, despite the English club facing sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The Premier League said City had used [USN:L6N45L10S TEXT:""sham" commercial contracts"] as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion). City, who have denied wrongdoing throughout the case and have [USN:L1N45O0BQ TEXT:"appealed the verdict"], could face punishments ranging from fines and a points deduction, to relegation and potentially being stripped of their titles. Asked about the verdict before PSG's Champions League match against City, Luis Enrique told a press conference on Tuesday: "The first thing when you hear that, it's a surprise, but I think we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision. "There are authorities responsible for making that decision, these decisions, and we have to wait, but if I speak only about football and the things that I saw on the pitch, Man City deserve those trophies. "I love the way they play football, and after that, you have to wait (for the) last decision and nothing else ... I think the trophies that you win on the pitch remains on the pitch, and they deserve to win that. I hope they can avoid that sanction." City host PSG at the Etihad Stadium later on Wednesday. ($1 = 0.7535 pounds)

item.title: Morning Bid: Let the doves sing
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rocky Swift
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rocky Swift With US Federal Reserve officials singing a less hawkish tune overnight, Singapore kept the dovish trend rolling with a surprise hold on policy. All 10 analysts polled by Reuters had expected the Monetary Authority of Singapore to tighten monetary settings on Wednesday. But instead, the MAS [USN:L6N46000E TEXT:"kept"] policy on hold on the view that growth and inflation would ease. So maybe the energy shock to prices isn't so bad? Or we perhaps just need more data? On the data front, the main event is the US Labor Department's reading for the September consumer price index. Analysts on average estimated a 0.6% month-on-month rise versus 0.4% in August, with annual inflation accelerating to 3.6% from 3.4%. Additionally, the Fed is due to publish its Beige Book report on how US regional economies are faring as policymakers debate the need for more tightening. New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said overnight he still sees one more interest rate [USN:L6N45Z14X TEXT:"hike"] this year but downplayed the need to lift again in 2027. Traders see a 77% chance that the Fed will leave its policy rate unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 51% a month ago, while pricing in about 75 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The chorus of Fed speak continues with Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin scheduled to participate in a fireside chat in Virginia, while Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman is due to talk in Bangkok. The Thai capital is where it's at this week, with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank carrying on annual meetings there. Seemingly speaking to France, the IMF's Rodrigo Valdes said in Bangkok that the body had "dialled up" the urgency of its call for governments to rein in [USN:S0N43A00B TEXT:"debt"]. European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde was more [USN:L1N46002V TEXT:"direct"], saying France needed to solve its debt woes on its own. Earnings were mixed overnight from Citigroup (C.N) and other major financial groups. Wednesday brings results from BlackRock, Morgan Stanley and Bank of America, with analysts expecting all three to show increases in the third quarter. The source of all the inflation concern doesn't seem to be ebbing. Oil prices climbed in Asian trading following more [USN:L1N46000C TEXT:"attacks"] by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on Saudi Arabia. Iranian officials described new [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"tactics"] to target ships on the Strait of Hormuz to keep oil prices high. Elsewhere, China's export growth topped market forecasts in September, with [USN:L6N46005Q TEXT:"robust"] overseas demand helping offset weak consumer spending. In early European trade, the pan-region Euro Stoxx 50 futures were up 0.36%, German DAX futures rose 0.38%, and FTSE futures edged 0.07% higher. US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis , were up 0.22%. Key developments that could influence markets on Wednesday: US CPI, Fed Beige Book Germany: Reopening of 21-year and 30-year government debt auctions UK: Reopening of 4-year government debt auction

item.title: Trump says 'massive' oil, gas and mineral exploration to begin in Greenland
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive" oil, gas and mineral exploration is getting ready to begin in Greenland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that "massive" oil, gas and mineral exploration is getting ready to begin in Greenland. Trump did not share details about the exploration plans in Greenland but said, "there are experts that are saying that the amount of easily available oil is far greater than that of almost any land, anywhere in the world." The United States, Denmark and Greenland last month [USN:L6N45E07X TEXT:"signed"] an agreement, aimed at ending tensions after Trump's repeated threats to take control of the strategically located and mineral-rich island. "Any future attack on the United States will have to come across Greenland, where our Defense will routinely knock down drones, missiles, or any other form of weapon not yet even conceived," Trump added in his post on Truth Social. The deal signed between the US, Denmark and Greenland expands the [USN:L1N45D0X6 TEXT:"US military's role"] in Greenland, paving the way for two new military bases and Trump's "Golden Dome" missile defence system, while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.

item.title: Russian strikes kill one, hit energy facilities in Kyiv, mayor says

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian air strikes killed one person and injured one more in Kyiv while also hitting energy facilities in the Ukrainian capital, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Wednesday. The ballistic missile attack was ongoing during the morning hours. The fresh strikes [USN:L1N45Z11U TEXT:"follow"] earlier Russian attacks on the energy infrastructure in Ukraine as temperatures start to cool down with the heating season on the horizon. Reuters witnesses heard multiple explosions in Kyiv as air defences [USN:P8N44K00S TEXT:"repelled"] overnight attacks. In the Volga River town of Balakovo in Russia, which invaded Ukraine in 2022, drones killed one person and damaged houses, a regional governor [USN:P8N44K00R TEXT:"said"] on Telegram.

item.title: US to drop South Korea intelligence case against ex-CIA analyst
item.description: The US Justice Department has agreed to forgo prosecution of a former CIA analyst and White House National Security Council official who was accused of working as an unregistered agent for South Korea in exchange for luxury goods and other gifts.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department has agreed to forgo prosecution of a former CIA analyst and White House National Security Council official who was accused of working as an unregistered agent for South Korea in exchange for luxury goods and other gifts. Under a deferred prosecution deal reached with foreign policy specialist Sue Mi Terry, the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York said it would suspend criminal charges in the [USN:L1N3J80YP TEXT:"grand jury indictment"] returned against her in July 2024. Provided that Terry abides by several conditions stipulated in the deal, including restrictions on her travel and contacts with the government of South Korea, the case against her would be dropped altogether after 12 months of compliance. Terms of the agreement were laid out in a four-page deferred prosecution notice filed in US District Court in Manhattan on Tuesday. It gave Terry no explanation for why the Justice Department was essentially giving up its high-profile intelligence case except to say it had determined "that the interests of the United States and your own interest will be best served by deferring prosecution." The indictment accused Terry of accepting gifts from South Korea's government in return for advocating Seoul's policy positions, disclosing non-public information to its intelligence officers and facilitating access for South Korean government officials to their US counterparts. Her alleged work on behalf of South Korea as an unregistered foreign agent began in 2013, two years after she left US government employment, and ran for 10 years, including her time as a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations think tank. At the council, which placed her on unpaid leave following the indictment, she had worked as an expert on East Asia and Korean Peninsula. The indictment charged Terry with failing to register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, and conspiring to violate that law. Terry has maintained her innocence. Her lawyer, Lee Wolosky, said at the time that his client had been a harsh critic of the Seoul government and that she was being prosecuted for performing the work of an independent scholar and news analyst. The unexpected outcome spares Terry the immediate threat of a criminal conviction or any jail time. It comes weeks before the case was set to go to trial, according to the New York Times. "We have consistently maintained that her interactions with South Korean officials were conducted in furtherance of US interests and her work as a leading American specialist on North Korea and East Asia," the Times quoted Wolosky as saying in a statement about the agreement. As part of the deal, Terry admitted to no wrongdoing. But she acknowledged assisting South Korean intelligence officers in a number of ways, including sharing with them notes she had prepared for a meeting in 2022 between top State Department officials and Korea policy experts. She also admitted accepting designer handbags valued at more than $9,200, 19 meals at fine restaurants and $37,000 in payments to a public policy program on Korean affairs that she ran, as gifts from South Korean intelligence officers. Born in Seoul and raised in Virginia, Terry was a senior CIA analyst from 2001 to 2008, and director of Korean, Japan and Oceanic Affairs at the NSC from 2008 to 2009 under Republican President George W. Bush and Democratic President Barack Obama.

item.title: IMF's Georgieva says US growth will not be enough to shrink debt
item.description: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt and needs to make other fiscal adjustments to put its debt on a more sustainable path, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States cannot grow its way out of mounting public debt and needs to make other fiscal adjustments to put its debt on a more sustainable path, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday. Georgieva told reporters at IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recognizes that US deficits and overall debt, now above $40 trillion, are too high. "The authorities very much rely on strong growth in the United States" to help reduce debt, Georgieva said. "At the Fund, we believe that growth of course helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments. So, some (fiscal) measures would be necessary."

item.title: Asia must guard against another financial crisis, Philippines central bank chief says
item.description: Asian countries must remind themselves about what happened during the region's financial crisis in the late 1990s and guard against a recurrence of such shocks, the head of the Philippine central bank said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Asian countries must remind themselves about what happened during the region's financial crisis in the late 1990s and guard against a recurrence of such shocks, the head of the Philippine central bank said on Wednesday. Before the Asian financial crisis started in 1997, regional economies saw huge capital inflows that prompted the World Bank to describe it as the "East Asian miracle," Eli Remolona, governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Philippines, said in an IMF panel on the outlook for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). "Investment poured into Asia, and then you had the crisis because it wasn't really a miracle. I think we have to remind ourselves about that. We have to guard against that kind of crisis," he said. "We have not really been making a lot of effort looking at that kind of crisis." The remarks came at the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank being held in Bangkok, Thailand, which was an [USN:L4N45R0MD TEXT:"epicentre"] of the Asian financial crisis. Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific Department, pushed back against the view, arguing in the panel discussion that the IMF has made progress assessing financial vulnerabilities and potential spillovers among each economy. "We have taken (the crisis) to heart, and we've dealt with a framework to talk about how should countries deal with volatile capital flows in terms ... such as when should they intervene in foreign exchange markets and so on," Srinivasan said. Srinivasan also said while ASEAN economies have weathered the trade tensions caused by US tariffs fairly well, their energy intensity could be among risks to the outlook as some countries rely heavily on oil and gas imports. Atsushi Mimura, Japan's vice finance minister for international affairs, also cited the energy shock from the Middle East conflict, as well as rising inflation, as among short-term risks to the region's outlook. "Of course, we all know that (fiscal support) should be 'triple T' - targeted, tailored and temporary," Mimura said on how economies should exercise discipline in delivering spending to cushion the blow to households and firms from the energy shock. As many countries face competitive pressure from China, ASEAN countries should focus on further strengthening investment to diversify supply chains in critical minerals and energy, Mimura said, a drive Japan was willing to support. "All ASEAN countries should definitely further invest so that they can always catch up with AI and innovation," Mimura told the panel. "At the same time, I think ASEAN countries are really well positioned in the supply chain for digitalisation because they're producing critical minerals." The 11-member ASEAN bloc comprises Brunei, Cambodia, East Timor, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

item.title: Financial Stability Board should concentrate on genuinely systemic risks, review finds
item.description: The Financial Stability Board, the global watchdog for financial risks, should be more selective in prioritising new work and focus on vulnerabilities that are genuinely cross-border, cross-sectoral and systemic, a review of its processes found.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Financial Stability Board, the global watchdog for financial risks, should be more selective in prioritising new work and focus on vulnerabilities that are genuinely cross-border, cross-sectoral and systemic, a review of its processes found. The review, the findings of which were published on Wednesday, was commissioned to examine whether the FSB's approach to developing, drafting and presenting policy has itself created obstacles to implementation. It was conducted by the Independent Monitoring Review (IMR) group chaired by Randal Quarles, a former FSB chair and former US Federal Reserve vice chair for supervision and follows a 2025 report that noted a " concerning trend " of delayed or stalled implementation of FSB recommendations. The IMR found that national factors, including legal frameworks, market structures and political capacity, were the main reasons why implementation has lagged. It said the FSB's own processes had not always sufficiently accounted for those circumstances, in some cases making implementation more difficult or more contentious than necessary. The FSB should default to high-level principles when a vulnerability is still emerging, adding more detailed requirements only as its understanding of the risks develops, the IMR added. The FSB's recent work has included recommendations to improve cross-border payments and for the supervision of global stablecoins. It is also developing non-binding guidance for practices on AI use. Also on Wednesday, the FSB proposed eight recommendations that aim to modernise supervision frameworks.

item.title: High gasoline prices expected to boost US consumer inflation in September
item.description: US consumer prices likely surged in September, driven by rising gasoline and food costs, and adding to a string of unfavorable developments for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party heading into crucial November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: US consumer prices likely surged in September, driven by rising gasoline and food costs, and adding to a string of unfavorable developments for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party heading into crucial November 3 midterm elections. The Labor Department's Consumer Price Index report on Wednesday will follow in the wake of surveys showing a deterioration in [USN:AQN2MNK41 TEXT:"consumer sentiment"] and a decline in Trump's [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"approval rating"] amid frustration over the rising cost of living. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed about 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blamed Trump's"] policies, including tariffs on imports and the US-Israeli war with Iran, for rising prices, which are outpacing wages. The CPI report is, however, expected to show a moderate increase in prices outside the volatile food and energy components over September, and further reduce the urgency for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again this month. Economists said the slowdown in the monthly so-called core CPI inflation was of little comfort to consumers, especially those at the bottom of what they call the K-shaped economy. "People care about food and energy. That's what they feel every day," said Sung Won Sohn, a finance and economics professor at Loyola Marymount University. "Many voters are at the lower leg of the K-shaped economy. They are suffering because of higher energy and food prices, and I assume that will have an impact on the election results, as a lot of people seem to think." The CPI likely increased 0.6% last month after climbing 0.4% in August, a Reuters survey of economists predicted. Some estimated that gasoline could add roughly three-tenths of a percentage point to the CPI. Gasoline prices soared 7.1% in September, data from the US Energy Information Administration showed. Food prices are expected to have risen at least 0.2% after two straight monthly gains of 0.1%. In the 12 months through September, the CPI is forecast to have increased 3.6% after rising 3.4% in August. The US central bank tracks the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Indexes for its 2% inflation target. The September CPI inflation report will be keenly awaited by millions of retirees and other Social Security recipients trying to figure out how much their benefits will increase next year. The Social Security Administration uses the CPI for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers data from the third quarter of 2025 to the third quarter of 2026 to determine the annual cost-of-living adjustment for Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits for 2027. The programs benefit older Americans who have retired as well as the disabled and certain widows, widowers and children. The Senior Citizens League, one of the nation's biggest seniors groups, is projecting a 3.5% COLA raise in 2027. That would be up from 2.8% in 2026, and would lift the average monthly benefit for retirees by $67.90 to $2,007. ENERGY PRICES SHOCK The energy price shock is being closely watched for signs of broadening out beyond the transportation sector. Some economists said more expensive energy products were yet to become embedded into inflation, citing moderate increases in the core CPI. Others warned record high diesel prices, with no end in sight to the Middle East conflict, would soon feed through to higher prices at the supermarket. They pointed to elevated readings in the price measures in business surveys. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI is expected to have gained 0.2% in September after climbing 0.3% in August. The anticipated moderation in core CPI inflation over the month would reflect the fading boost from a jump in mobile phone prices related to service changes at AT&T, though an above-expectations increase could not be ruled out. Other service providers raised their fees in September. Airline fares likely increased further because of rising jet fuel prices. Moderate rises are expected for rents. Goods prices likely rose marginally as the impact of tariffs unwinds. In the 12 months through September, core CPI inflation is forecast to have increased 2.5% after advancing 2.4% in August. This measure is lagging core PCE inflation, which increased 3.0% in August, because of the different weights assigned to the components in the baskets. The Fed last month raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead. Financial markets assigned a roughly 22% chance of a rate hike at the October 27-28 policy meeting, CME's FedWatch Tool showed. The odds of a rate increase this month were diminished by the [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"underwhelming payroll"] gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected PCE [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation readings"] for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December. "If the monthly core CPI rise manages to stay in the 0.2% range in September, that should be good enough for the Fed to hold in October," said Scott Anderson, chief US economist at BMO Capital Markets. "However, it won't settle the debate about whether more rate hikes are needed down the road."

item.title: Singapore MPA builds capability to supply various bunker fuels
item.description: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said on Wednesday it is expanding the world's largest bunkering port's ability to supply a wider range of fuels as shipping firms diversify fuel sources and pursue decarbonisation goals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) said on Wednesday it is expanding the world's largest bunkering port's ability to supply a wider range of fuels as shipping firms diversify fuel sources and pursue decarbonisation goals. MPA will invite bids from companies by end-2026 for licences to operate liquefied natural gas Floating Storage Units (FSUs) in Singapore anchorages, expanding storage capacity to meet rising LNG bunkering demand. MPA, CMA CGM and Singapore LNG Corp signed a memorandum of understanding to explore the use of liquefied bio-methane as a marine fuel. Singapore will conduct its first ethanol bunkering operation at PSA’s Pasir Panjang Terminal later this week, involving Maersk, Golden Island Pte Ltd and PSA Singapore. To support ammonia bunkering, MPA and Enterprise Singapore have launched a technical reference setting out safety requirements, bunkering procedures, custody transfer standards and competency requirements for personnel. The Singapore Chamber of Maritime Arbitration (SCMA) is also developing a model contract for ammonia bunkering transactions. MPA will accelerate the use of electric harbour craft by introducing a two-year grant for early adopters from January 1, 2027.

item.title: US Justice Department threatens California over alleged noncitizen voters, letter shows
item.description: The US Justice Department on Tuesday gave California officials 48 hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters - part of an unprecedented effort to find evidence of voter fraud ahead of next month's elections.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage , Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department on Tuesday gave California officials 48 hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action, according to a letter reviewed by Reuters - part of an unprecedented effort to find evidence of voter fraud ahead of next month's elections. The letter, written by acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter and addressed to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber, says the Justice Department provided officials in Los Angeles County with a "password-protected thumb drive" with the names of people the federal government "believes are likely noncitizens" and were sent mail-in ballots. The letter demands that the state refuse to send ballots to those on the list until their citizenship status has been confirmed. Voters in question who have already received ballots should have their ballot "segregated" once it is mailed back; ballots already returned should not be tabulated "until citizenship has been determined," the letter stipulates. The federal government "will have no choice but to seek emergency relief," according to the letter, if state officials do not follow its instructions. "Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes," McCotter wrote. The letter marks an escalation of the Trump administration's attempts to pressure states over alleged voting by non-US citizens and signals the Justice Department may be prepared to challenge ballots in the weeks leading up to the November 3 election, when Republicans will be defending their narrow majorities in Congress. Justice Department spokeswoman Kiersten Pels confirmed the existence of the letter in a statement to Reuters, adding: "The department will take all necessary legal action to protect election integrity and ensure compliance with federal law.” Representatives from the White House and the California secretary of state's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. FRAUD CLAIMS The Justice Department under President Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed that voting by non-US citizens is widespread, despite multiple studies showing it is rare. Though states may have added more than [USN:L6N43Z058 TEXT:"30,000 noncitizens to their voter rolls"] since 2000 due to software glitches and clerical errors, Reuters found in September, it was unclear how many had cast a ballot. Experts said the numbers were too small relative to the country’s 170 million registered voters to affect elections. In July, the Justice Department [USN:L6N43A182 TEXT:"sent letters"] to chief election officials in all 50 states warning they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls or cast ballots. The department's Civil Rights Division has demanded nonpublic voter data, including voters' Social Security numbers or dates of birth, from nearly all states as part of its hunt for noncitizens on state rolls. It has [USN:L6N44118V TEXT:"sued"] 30 Democratic- and Republican-led states that refused to hand over their rolls, but has [USN:S0N3R907R TEXT:"lost 26 of those cases"] without winning one. Reuters [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"reported"] last month that the Department of Homeland Security was using a commercial data broker to find sensitive voter information not included in publicly available rolls, which officials and experts warned could lead to citizens being falsely flagged as illegal voters and potentially detained. Federal prosecutors have also [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"ramped up"] prosecutions of noncitizens for allegedly voting in past elections or submitting fraudulent registrations, touting 16 new criminal cases on Monday. Officials in Democratic-led California have tussled for months with the Trump administration over its attempts to intervene in election procedures over allegations of voter fraud. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin informed California officials on July 16 that the federal government believed the state had noncitizens on its voting rolls, according to the letter. California could prove pivotal in deciding control of the US House of Representatives, especially after the state's voters approved a new congressional map that heavily favors Democrats as part of a nationwide redistricting sprint that began in Republican-led states. Voters in Los Angeles will also weigh in on a ballot measure that would allow certain noncitizen legal residents to cast ballots in municipal elections.

item.title: Golden Knights stay hot, pull away from Predators
item.description: William Karlsson scored the tiebreaking goal late in the second period Tuesday night to spark a three-goal surge for the Vegas Golden Knights, who beat the host Nashville Predators 5-2.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: William Karlsson scored the tiebreaking goal late in the second period Tuesday night to spark a three-goal surge for the Vegas Golden Knights, who beat the host Nashville Predators 5-2. Tomas Hertl and Jack Eichel scored in the first period, while Trevor Connelly and Brett Howden added insurance in the third for the Golden Knights, who have won five of their last six and lead the Western Conference with 12 points. Goalie Adin Hill made 25 saves, including a Jack Drury penalty shot with 6:51 left in the first to maintain Vegas' 2-1 lead. Ryan O'Reilly had a goal and an assist and Adam Edstrom also scored for the Predators, who have dropped four of their first six. Goalie Juuse Saros recorded 20 saves. O'Reilly opened the scoring 3:55 into the first, when he picked off a pass by Shea Theodore and dished to Filip Forsberg before swooping in and backhanding home the rebound. A Predators turnover led to Hertl's goal a little under three minutes later. Howden intercepted a pass by Ross Colton to begin the sequence that ended with Hertl firing a shot over Saros' glove shoulder at the 6:46 mark. An impressive effort by Eichel gave the Golden Knights their first lead with 7:12 left in the first. Brayden McNabb passed into the crease, where Eichel extended his right arm and flicked the puck past Saros. Edstrom tied the game with a short-handed goal 8:45 into the second, when he retrieved the rebound from his breakaway attempt and poked a shot around Hill and into the far corner of the net. Karlsson put the Golden Knights ahead for good nine minutes later, when he took a feed from Mitch Marner and beat Saros over his stick shoulder from the right faceoff circle. Vegas doubled the lead 4:49 into the third. Noah Hanifin passed from the goal line to Connelly, whose shot went over Saros' glove. Howden added insurance 1:35 later. --Field Level Media

item.title: Singapore marine fuel supplier Equatorial eyes higher LNG bunker demand from 2028
item.description: Equatorial Marine Fuel Management, a top Singapore bunker supplier by volume, plans to channel part of its 2026 profits to fund its expansion into supplying liquefied natural gas to ships as it positions for higher demand from 2028, its executives said.
item.dc:creator: Jeslyn Lerh
item.content:encoded: Equatorial Marine Fuel Management, a top Singapore bunker supplier by volume, plans to channel part of its 2026 profits to fund its expansion into supplying liquefied natural gas to ships as it positions for higher demand from 2028, its executives said. The company, which was one of eight suppliers [USN:L1N43W0ED TEXT:"awarded"] an LNG bunker licence in late July, is in discussions with LNG cargo suppliers and shipowners for collaborations, its executive director Choong Zhen Mao told Reuters on the sidelines of the Singapore International Bunkering conference. "The opportunity that we see in LNG still seems to be growing, even in this climate. I think that's where we see the market moving," he said, referring to the surge in LNG prices after the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted exports from the Middle East. The company will be receiving its first new-built LNG bunker barge in the later part of the third quarter in 2027, he added. Equatorial's chief operating officer, Choong Sheen Mao, expects a more notable increase in Singapore's LNG bunker demand from 2028 as more LNG production capacity and dual-fuel vessels come online globally. Equatorial currently supplies about 10% of total bunker volumes at Singapore, the world's biggest refuelling hub for ships, according to its executives. The city state has supplied an average 4.7 million tons of bunker fuel a month so far in 2026, official data show. The company's year-to-date profits for 2026 have exceeded last year's level, the executives said, though they did not disclose the figures. Bunker fuel prices surged after US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February drove oil prices higher, and have remained volatile since then. The ensuing disruption to shipping routes supported refuelling demand in key hubs including Singapore. "Demand looks to be resilient," said ED Choong. "When there is uncertainty, sometimes people tend to purchase a bit more, fill their tanks a bit more... people tend to break a voyage down into smaller trades these days to ensure availability and cargo security." Equatorial owns eight fuel oil barges, seven marine gasoil barges, as well as four chemical bunker tankers that meet International Maritime Organization's type 2 standard to carry methanol or biofuel blends up to 100% biofuel content. Some of the chemical bunker barges have been repurposed to supply conventional fuel this year amid a slowdown in marine biofuel demand, COO Choong said. "Demand for biofuels has slowed this year because of the delay in the IMO's net-zero framework, while current prices are not competitive," he said. Depending on the blend and delivery window, biofuel blends command premiums of at least $100 per metric ton over conventional low-sulphur bunker fuel oil, according to industry sources.

item.title: Liverpool boss Iraola has 100% trust in Wirtz and Barcola
item.description: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has no doubts that big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola will deliver for the club and says their contributions to the side are being overlooked due to the constant focus on their transfer fees.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has no doubts that big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola will deliver for the club and says their contributions to the side are being overlooked due to the constant focus on their transfer fees. Liverpool spent over £200 million ($265 million) to acquire the pair but both have come in for criticism. Wirtz had an underwhelming 2025-26 campaign and has just one assist this season, while [USN:L6N44S0QI TEXT:"Barcola"], who arrived in August, has yet to produce a goal or an assist. "With Bradley and Flo, they have had good games and bad games this season like everyone else," Iraola told reporters on Tuesday ahead of their Champions League meeting with LASK. "We know their level and we know they will give us good performances. "The other day, if Lewis Koumas scores the goal that he connects with really well (in their [USN:L1N45X053 TEXT:"3-0 loss to Manchester City"]), then it is one assist for Bradley Barcola. "His performance would be exactly the same but we will all say: 'Oh, he played really well with an assist.' Sometimes we focus only on the numbers. "With Bradley, the other day he had good situations and we did not finish them. Bradley and Flo are players that I trust 100%." Liverpool face LASK in Linz later on Wednesday, before travelling to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. ($1 = 0.7539 pounds)

item.title: Martin Necas, Avalanche surge ahead, hold off Stars
item.description: Martin Necas had two goals, Mackenzie Blackwood bounced back from a difficult outing to make 24 saves, and the visiting Colorado Avalanche beat the Dallas Stars 3-2 in the first game of a home-and-home set Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Martin Necas had two goals, Mackenzie Blackwood bounced back from a difficult outing to make 24 saves, and the visiting Colorado Avalanche beat the Dallas Stars 3-2 in the first game of a home-and-home set Tuesday night. Artturi Lehkonen also scored and Nathan MacKinnon had two assists and also fought for the second time in the first six games for Colorado. The teams play again Wednesday night in Denver. The Avalanche were without All-Star defenseman Cale Makar and forward Zachary L'Heureux. Makar stayed in Colorado to be with his wife, who was expecting twins, while L'Heureux was a late scratch due to an upper-body injury. Dallas played without center Wyatt Johnston, who was also a late scratch with an illness. Johnston had played the full 82-game regular-season schedule each of his first four NHL seasons as well as the Stars' first five games this season. The Stars' Tyler Seguin had a goal and an assist and Roope Hintz also scored to go along with his fight with MacKinnon in the second period. The scuffle opened a cut on the bridge of MacKinnon's nose, and he went to the locker room for nearly eight minutes before returning. Miro Heiskanen had two assists and Jake Oettinger turned away 22 shots for Dallas. The Avalanche took the lead midway through the first period when Josh Manson's shot from the point hit MacKinnon's skate, back to Lehkonen, who knocked it past Oettinger at 11:32. Seguin tied it on the power play in the final minute of the first with his second goal in as many games. Colorado answered in the second period. Necas gave the Avalanche the lead when he took a backhand pass from MacKinnon and beat Oettinger with a one-timer at 3:05. Necas made it 3-1 when he scored on a 5-on-3 at 16:14. Blackwood, who allowed five goals on 22 shots in a 6-3 home loss to Toronto on Saturday, kept it a two-goal advantage heading into the second intermission when he stoned Sam Steel on a point-blank shot after a turnover by Colorado defenseman Sam Malinski. Hintz got the Stars within a goal when he scored 3:17 into the third. Oettinger came off for an extra skater with 1:49 left but Dallas couldn't score. --Field Level Media

item.title: Austal shares jump as Hanwha gets more time to bid for US unit
item.description: Australian shipbuilder Austal said on Wednesday it had extended the due diligence period for Hanwha Group, allowing the South Korean conglomerate more time to formulate a formal offer for its US business, sending its shares sharply higher.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australian shipbuilder Austal (ASB.AX) said on Wednesday it had extended the due diligence period for Hanwha Group, allowing the South Korean conglomerate more time to formulate a formal offer for its US business, sending its shares sharply higher. Here are some details: Austal said commercial negotiations with Hanwha had started on the terms of a potential transaction, while the company also continues to assess its tax implications. Austal shares jumped as much as 11.5% to A$4.18 by 0315 GMT, posting their strongest intraday gain since August 11. "Regarding due diligence, while the substantive issues in the data room have been closed out, and the original parameters of the transaction have not changed, a tail of lower materiality data requests remains outstanding," Austal said in a statement. The company said it also remains in discussions with US-based Wildcat Infrastructure regarding its proposal to acquire Austal's US operations. Wildcat Infrastructure [USN:L4N45101Q TEXT:"in September"] offered up to $1.35 billion for Austal's US business, topping an earlier bid of up to $1.20 billion from Hanwha.

item.title: Report: Alex DeBrincat, Red Wings finalizing 7-year contract extension
item.description: Forward Alex DeBrincat and the Detroit Red Wings are finalizing a seven-year contract extension valued at $13 million annually, ESPN reported on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Forward Alex DeBrincat and the Detroit Red Wings are finalizing a seven-year contract extension valued at $13 million annually, ESPN reported on Tuesday night. DeBrincat leads the Red Wings with eight points, four goals, four assists and a plus-7 rating in six games after he scored twice and added an assist in their 5-4 overtime loss at home to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday. The 28-year-old was eligible for a contract extension this summer, before the new collective bargaining agreement started in September. The former maximum for a contract was eight years; now it is seven. For his career, DeBrincat has 603 points (298 goals, 305 assists), 198 penalty minutes, 281 blocks and 557 hits in 702 regular-season games for the Chicago Blackhawks (2017-22), Ottawa Senators (2022-23) and Red Wings (2023-present). An All-Star in 2022 and 2024, he also has six points (two goals, four assists), nine penalty minutes, three blocks and 13 hits in nine playoff games with Chicago in the 2019-20 season. Chicago selected DeBrincat in the second round of the 2016 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: IMF's Georgieva optimistic on Senegal debt treatment under improved G20 framework
item.description: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday that she was optimistic that Senegal would be able to renegotiate its debts, and that would demonstrate that improvements to the G20 debt treatment framework are working.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said on Wednesday that she was optimistic that Senegal would be able to renegotiate its debts, and that would demonstrate that improvements to the G20 debt treatment framework are working. She told a briefing at IMF and World Bank annual meetings that the IMF would support Senegal with a staff-negotiated agreement for a $2.2 billion program, but the debt treatment was being worked out between Senegal and its creditors. "I can tell you that my conversations with key creditors indicate everybody understands this is the test case to the playbook we have adopted through the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable," she said. "It is very important that we demonstrate that yes, indeed, the G20 common framework is improved, enhanced, and it can deliver results quickly. Senegal deserves it."

item.title: India's 'cockroach' movement leaders detained in jail for five days, party says
item.description: The detentions risk triggering fresh protests by youth supporters at a time when opposition groups and student bodies are holding almost daily demonstrations to demand election chief Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter list revisions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Indian court ordered that two leaders of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) be detained in jail for five days, the party said on Wednesday, a day after they scaled barricades to enter a historic site popular for protests and chanted slogans demanding the election chief's resignation. The detentions risk triggering fresh protests by youth supporters at a time when opposition groups and student bodies are holding almost daily demonstrations to demand commissioner [USN:P8N44T0DC TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation over [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"voter list revisions"] that critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were among about a dozen people who [USN:L6N45Z0LD TEXT:"jumped barricades "]on Tuesday to enter the grounds of the Jantar Mantar open air observatory in Delhi's central business district. Police said this week that the site -- previously designated for demonstrations -- was no longer an official protest venue. Das and Ranka were sent to prison on grounds including violation of a bond which had secured their release from an earlier detention on the weekend, their lawyer Abhisht Hela told reporters. "Delhi Police said they had violated their bond, and that they could do this again...that what they have done is a violation of law," he said. WILL NOT BE FRIGHTENED, CJP SAYS CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde, who was released on a personal bond, said the party would not be "frightened" by its leaders' imprisonment. "We will put an end to this dictatorial government," he said. Delhi Police did not respond to a request for comment. The 'cockroach' movement has mobilised protests in recent months against issues ranging from government school infrastructure to jobs and is among Modi and his BJP's biggest political challenges in his 12 years in power. A [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"weeks-long sit-in "]by its supporters at Jantar Mantar earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks. The recent demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about the changes, registration procedures and digital systems. The revisions, which started last year, removed over 130 million names – more than the population of Japan – from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslims and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party — allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

item.title: Taiwan must 'bear the consequences' of water cannon incident, China says
item.description: Taiwan must "bear the consequences" of its Coast Guard using a water cannon against a Chinese fishing boat near an atoll in the South China Sea, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, as Taipei reported a rise in military activities.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Taiwan must "bear the consequences" of its Coast Guard using a water cannon against a Chinese fishing boat near an atoll in the South China Sea, a Chinese government spokesperson said on Wednesday, as Taipei reported a rise in military activities. A Taiwan Coast Guard ship this month fired its water cannon, saying the boat failed to respond to warnings to move away from restricted waters close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands. The boat then suffered engine failure and was towed away by a nearby Chinese vessel, Taiwan's Coast Guard said. Chen Binhua, a spokesperson for China's Taiwan Affairs Office in Beijing, said China has "indisputable sovereignty" over the Pratas and surrounding waters. "Mainland vessels operating in the relevant waters are entirely legal and justified. We will resolutely safeguard the lives and property of our people," Chen said. Taiwan's "treatment of mainland vessels roughly in a dangerous manner that endangers the lives and property of the personnel involved is maliciously stirring up cross-strait confrontation and they must bear all consequences arising from this," Chen said, without elaborating on the consequences. A Taiwan official with direct knowledge of the situation around the Pratas told Reuters that the Coast Guard carried out "normal law enforcement" during the incident and responded in a "very careful and proportionate way". The Pratas Islands lie roughly between southern Taiwan and Hong Kong. Security experts see them as vulnerable to Chinese attack due to their distance — more than 400 km (250 miles) — from Taiwan. China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and has increased its military presence around the island over the past five years. The government in Taipei rejects China's claim. China recognises no claims of sovereignty by Taiwan, including over the Pratas Islands, and Chinese coast guard ships have increased patrols. 'GREY ZONE' ACTIVITIES Taiwan says China is increasing its "grey zone" tactics that stop short of outright military action to pressure Taiwan. Speaking at a forum in Taipei, Lii Wen, deputy secretary-general of Taiwan's National Security Council, said China was using a wider range of ships in its "incremental acts of aggression," including militia boats and research vessels. "Grey zone activities under the threshold of conflict have raised serious concerns for their potential to disrupt transportation or damage critical infrastructure," he added. Underscoring the threat Taiwan says it faces, Taiwan's defence ministry flagged another "joint combat readiness patrol" by China near the island on Wednesday, with 13 aircraft including J-16 fighters and an unspecified number of navy ships. China's defence ministry said earlier in the day that the aircraft carrier Liaoning and accompanying ships were drilling in the Western Pacific, though it did not give details. Taiwan's Coast Guard is in charge of day-to-day security for Pratas rather than the military. The Pratas Islands are a national park. They have an airstrip but no permanent civilian population.

item.title: ECB's Lagarde says solution to French debt woes is at home
item.description: France should solve its own debt woes through fiscal policy consolidation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Wednesday, effectively playing down speculation about an ECB intervention in the bond market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France should solve its own debt woes through fiscal policy consolidation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said on Wednesday, effectively playing down speculation about an ECB intervention in the bond market. French government bonds have been [USN:L8N45S1P0 TEXT:"among the worst hit"] by a global selloff, with investors concerned that political jostling ahead of next year's presidential election may hinder the government's efforts to reduce its high deficit. Asked whether the ECB was about to help France, Lagarde said it was up to Paris to soothe investors' nerves. "There are particular circumstances that lead to some countries being more affected, France being a case in point," she told a CNN event in Bangkok. "And for that one, the primary and first solution lies at home in France. And it has to do with fiscal policies." Analysts have been speculating for weeks about whether the ECB might start buying French bonds via a crisis-fighting tool known as the Transmission Protection Instrument. This can be activated if a country is under market pressure that the ECB deems "unwarranted", "disorderly" and threatening the transmission of the central bank's interest rates to all corners of the euro zone. ECB LOOKS FOR INFLATION 'HINTS', GROWTH IS 'NOT BAD' Asked about monetary policy, Lagarde said the current, high rate of inflation in the euro zone had been driven "predominantly, but not exclusively" by a surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war. While there was no sign yet of "second-round effects" on other prices, the ECB would be looking for "hints", such as trade unions' demands in wage negotiations. "We cannot wait until they're there in full view, but we can anticipate," she said at the event on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in the Thai capital. "So we very carefully follow those entry points." The ECB [USN:L1N45U0EF TEXT:"has raised rates"] twice in the past four months and is expected to do so again in December. Lagarde said the 1.1% increase in GDP expected by the IMF for the euro zone this year was "not brilliant" but "not a bad outcome" either and flagged continued support from German government spending on infrastructure and the military.

item.title: Judge extends White House access for CNN, MS NOW, Politico amid legal fight
item.description: A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them, in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute.
item.dc:creator: Jack Queen, Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: A federal judge extended access to the White House for CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists, deciding on Tuesday that President Donald Trump likely broke the law when he tried to ban them, in the latest ruling against him in the press freedom dispute. US District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a written decision that elaborated on his September 24 emergency order that reinstated access for the journalists. The news organizations and press freedom groups have accused Trump of unconstitutional retaliation against journalists for coverage he does not like. Kelly's order last month gave the CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists access to the White House grounds on a temporary basis. The judge issued a ruling called a preliminary injunction on Tuesday that will remain in effect until he makes a final judgment in the lawsuit brought by the news organizations, unless an appeals court lifts his order. Kelly wrote that Trump's public remarks made clear that he banned the news outlets because he considered their reporting biased and inaccurate, and not because of national security concerns as government lawyers later asserted in court. "Simply put, that is unlawful viewpoint discrimination," the judge wrote, adding that "no one should read this decision as suggesting that President Trump’s complaints are meritless." Trump appointed Kelly in 2017 during his first presidential term. CAMPAIGN AGAINST THE MEDIA Past presidents have battled with the press, but Trump's campaign against the media has been unprecedented. He has upended decades of tradition by denying basic access to many major news organizations, launching personal attacks on journalists for their reporting and elevating media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He also has filed lawsuits against multiple news outlets. Trump announced the ban in September on his social media platform, saying CNN, Politico, and MS NOW "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." The Justice Department has emphasized Trump's contention that the ban is legally justified on national security grounds. The outlets have said the revocation of their White House passes was unlawful retaliation for their news coverage and accused the Trump administration of manufacturing meritless national security concerns to justify the ban.
