The outlets said in a lawsuit that the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for freedom of speech and a free press, as well as their rights to due process, meaning fair treatment from the government. The White House on September 24 reinstated the CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists after Kelly decided the ban "likely violated their constitutional due process rights," and ordered their access immediately restored. 'COERCE BETTER COVERAGE' The judge held a hearing on October 8 to hear arguments by the news outlets and the Justice Department over whether to extend the protection for the journalists against being barred from the White House. The Justice Department defended the bans as fair and justified. "Here we have the unusual situation where the president himself has said he wants to chill speech. He wants to coerce better coverage," Theodore Boutrous, an attorney for the outlets, told Kelly during the hearing. "CNN, MS NOW and Politico engaged in apparently indefensible conduct," Justice Department lawyer Michael Velchik said. The legal battle is being waged just weeks before the November 3 US midterm elections in which Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress. Trump's job approval ratings are at record lows in opinion polls amid concerns over issues such as inflation and the Iran war.

item.title: Gold holds firm ahead of US inflation data
item.description: Gold prices held firm on Wednesday as investors braced for US consumer price index data due later in the day for clues on the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy stance.
item.dc:creator: Sukanya Mitra
item.content:encoded: Gold prices held firm on Wednesday as investors braced for US consumer price index data due later in the day for clues on the Federal Reserve's latest monetary policy stance. Spot gold held its ground at $4,165.25 per ounce, as of 0447 GMT. U.S. gold futures for December delivery edged 0.3% higher to $4,188.70. "What we're looking at here is not a big move, it's within a range. But the fact that we are able to hold a range while oil is rallying suggests that gold is trying to find a reason to rally," said Ilya Spivak, head of global macro at Tastylive. On the geopolitical front, an administrative building belonging to [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Arabia's"] state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked, the Energy Ministry said, as fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified. Oil prices [USN:L1N46000C TEXT:"scaled higher"] on the news on Wednesday. If upcoming consumer price index data, producer price index data and retail sales data point to weaker economic momentum, markets may scale back expectations for further Fed rate hikes this year, providing a bullish catalyst for gold, Spivak added. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report is due at 1230 GMT, followed by the Producer Price Index (PPI) and retail sales data on Thursday. New York Fed President [USN:L6N45Z14X TEXT:"John Williams"] reaffirmed his view that the US central bank may need to raise interest rates once more this year in its bid to lower inflation. Meanwhile, Fed Governor [USN:L1N45Z0AY TEXT:"Christopher Waller"] said the recent rise in US bond yields reflects stronger economic growth rather than higher inflation expectations, which remain "well-anchored". Markets are pricing in about a 22% chance of a US rate hike this month and an 88% probability of an increase in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool. Although gold is typically seen as a hedge against inflation, higher interest rates tend to diminish the appeal of non-yielding bullion to investors. Among other metals, spot silver dipped 0.2% to $59.33 per ounce, platinum steadied at $1,663.16 and palladium gained 0.7% to $1,133.49.

item.title: Rays capitalize on Guardians' error, knot ALCS behind Freddy Peralta
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays took advantage of an uncharacteristic error by Jose Ramirez to even their American League Championship Series against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays took advantage of an uncharacteristic error by Jose Ramirez to even their American League Championship Series against the Cleveland Guardians on Tuesday. Ramirez's miscue opened the door for a three-run frame in the fourth and Freddy Peralta tossed six scoreless innings, fueling the Rays to a 3-1 victory in Game 2 of the best-of-seven series. Liam Hicks recorded a two-run single and joined Jonny DeLuca with two hits for Tampa Bay. Game 3 of the best-of-seven series is Thursday in Cleveland. Peralta (1-0) scattered four hits and struck out six while walking two. The right-hander capped his 99-pitch outing by striking out rookie Petey Halpin to end the sixth. Peralta has allowed one or zero earned runs in eight consecutive outings. "I define myself as a competitor, and I like these kind of games," Peralta said. "... I grew up watching the games in (the Dominican Republic). That's the game that you see. And I'm used to that. I feel that I have that in me." Cleveland rookie Chase DeLauter ripped an RBI double down the right field line to trim Tampa Bay's lead to 3-1 in the seventh. Left-hander Ian Seymour, however, struck out Jo Adell with runners on second and third to end the inning. Seymour retired the side in order in the eighth to bridge the gap to All-Star closer Bryan Baker, who did the same in the ninth to secure his fourth save of the postseason after leading the major leagues with 41 in the regular season. "Makes for a happy flight. Mission accomplished on that front," Baker said. Ramirez misplayed a routine grounder by Ben Williamson, as the ball bounced through the third baseman's legs and into left field to allow Victor Mesa Jr. to score the game's first run in the fourth. "It's a little faster here," Ramirez said of the infield at Tropicana Field, through a club translator. "I was playing parallel to the base and the ball bounced right on the edge between the dirt and the turf. "I tried to knock it down, but I couldn't." Said Guardians manager Stephen Vogt: "Josey kind of got stuck. It looked like he just didn't move his feet. And I don't know if it hit the lip or not on the second hop, but just kind of looked like he sat back a little bit with his feet set instead of moving his feet." Hicks followed by sending the next pitch from All-Star rookie left-hander Parker Messick (0-2) into right-center field to plate Chandler Simpson and Williamson and stake Tampa Bay to a 3-0 lead. "I have to make it count. I have to make them pay for that," Hicks told MLB Network. "That's a team that doesn't make those types of errors. You have to take advantage of any kind of opportunity." Vogt credited the Rays for capitalizing. "They've done that all year. When they smell blood, they take it and run," he said. Earlier in the inning, the Guardians appeared to have turned their third double play in four innings before Tampa Bay successfully challenged the play. Mesa was ruled safe at first base. Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero snared a sharp liner by Steven Kwan in the fifth. Caminero then drew a rise out of the crowd by flashing a finger wag in the manner of former renowned NBA shot blocker Dikembe Mutombo. Messick, a native of nearby Plant City, Fla., permitted three runs (all unearned) on six hits in five innings. He also walked two and hit one batter. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jets' No. 1 line erupts for 7 points in win over Wild
item.description: Cole Perfetti scored a pair of goals, including the go-ahead tally, as the Winnipeg Jets pulled away for a 5-2 win over the visiting Minnesota Wild on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cole Perfetti scored a pair of goals, including the go-ahead tally, as the Winnipeg Jets pulled away for a 5-2 win over the visiting Minnesota Wild on Tuesday night. Perfetti and his No. 1 linemates, Mark Scheifele (one goal, two assists) and Kyle Connor (one goal, one assist), combined for seven points for Winnipeg, which won for the fourth time in its past five games. Neal Pionk added two assists. Kirill Kaprizov scored both goals for Minnesota, which lost in regulation for only the second time this season. Jets goaltender Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21 shots. Wild goaltender Calvin Pickard allowed five goals on 25 shots in his season debut. Winnipeg struck quickly with a goal 1:50 into the game. Pionk unleashed a wrist shot from near the blue line, and Perfetti deflected it just past Pickard's stick side and into the back of the net. The Wild evened the score with 11:13 remaining in the period. Kaprizov poked the puck loose from a Jets defender and headed to the crease on a mini-breakaway. His first shot was stopped but he scored on the rebound. The Jets regained a 2-1 lead with 2:06 left in the period. On the power play, Scheifele set up in the slot and scored his first goal of the season, a one-timer off a pinpoint pass from Pionk. Forty-four seconds later, Kaprizov struck again to even the score at 2-all. He redirected a shot from Quinn Hughes past Skinner for his NHL-leading eighth goal this season. Perfetti provided the go-ahead goal on the power play to make it 3-2 with 3:24 left in the second period. He scored from the slot on a one-timer for his fifth of the season. The Jets increased their lead to 4-2 with 15:54 remaining in the third. Connor carried the puck left to right, wheeled to his forehand and scored on a rising wrist shot for his seventh goal. Cole Koepke scored on a 2-on-1 rush to boost the Jets' lead to 5-2 with 5:18 left. -Field Level Media

item.title: China September rare earth exports rise 6.7% from a year earlier
item.description: China's exports of rare earths in September rose 6.7% from the prior year, customs data showed on Wednesday, as overseas buying improved after a summer lull.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's exports of rare earths in September rose 6.7% from the prior year, customs data showed on Wednesday, as overseas buying improved after a summer lull. The world's largest rare earth producer shipped out 4,269.8 metric tons of the group of 17 minerals essential to electric vehicles, wind turbines and defense technology, data from the General Administration of Customs showed. That was down 9.8% from 4,735 tons in [USN:L4N45007H TEXT:"August"] but was up from 4,000 tons in the [USN:L3N3VU073 TEXT:"same month in 2025"]. In the first nine months of 2026, total exports dropped 9.6% year-on-year to 43,711 tons.

item.title: Thyssenkrupp's largest shareholder sees 'window of opportunity' for steel spin-off
item.description: The head of the Krupp Foundation, the largest shareholder in German conglomerate Thyssenkrupp , believes there is currently a "window of opportunity" to spin off the firm's steel division, according to an interview published on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The head of the Krupp Foundation, the largest shareholder in German conglomerate Thyssenkrupp (TKAG.DE) , believes there is currently a "window of opportunity" to spin off the firm's steel division, according to an interview published on Wednesday. "I have the impression that there is currently a good window of opportunity for such a step," foundation head Ursula Gather said in the interview with the WAZ newspaper. She said she was optimistic due to Thyssenkrupp's [USN:L8N3US0CG TEXT:"restructuring deal"] with the IG Metall union, the [USN:L6N43B0KR TEXT:"sale of its stake"] in steelmaker HKM and [USN:L6N45A0Y0 TEXT:"additional protection"] for Europe's steel industry through EU tariffs. Gather has chaired the board of trustees of the Alfried Krupp von Bohlen und Halbach Foundation, which holds just under 21% of the company, since 2013. CEO Miguel Lopez plans to transform the Ruhr-based group into a financial holding company. He has already taken the hydrogen subsidiary Nucera (NCH2.DE) and defence company TKMS (TKMS.DE) public. Its materials trading subsidiary, tk accelis, is set to follow later this year.

item.title: Indian rupee to build on rally after RBI chief reinforces currency support
item.description: The Indian rupee is poised to extend its rally on Wednesday after the central bank's steps to support the currency were reinforced by the governor's indication that further measures remain an option.
item.dc:creator: Nimesh Vora
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is poised to extend its rally on Wednesday after the central bank's steps to support the currency were reinforced by the governor's indication that further measures remain an option. The rupee is expected to open in the 95.04-95.12 range, traders said, after settling at 95.28 to the dollar on Tuesday. The currency has already surged 1.5% over the past two sessions after the Reserve Bank of India rolled out a series of measures to address the dollar demand-supply imbalance that had kept the rupee under sustained pressure. In a media interview on Tuesday, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra defended the recent forex curbs as an effort to discourage speculative bets. He said the measures were meant to preserve access to currency hedges for businesses with genuine exposure, while signalling that the central bank is ready to take additional steps to ensure orderly rupee movement. Malhotra added that while monetary policy is not typically deployed to address financial stability concerns, the two cannot be entirely separated. "The mandate of price stability cannot be achieved without financial stability, as a stable financial system is essential for the effective transmission of monetary policy," Malhotra said. Bankers read Malhotra's comments as hawkish, with two saying they reinforced the case for a December rate hike, while one said the possibility of a 50 basis point increase was on the table. "The RBI is pulling out all the stops to break the rupee’s prolonged pressure," a currency trader at a bank said. "But the challenge is that the underlying fundamentals remain unfavourable," pointing to oil prices and weak capital flows. Oil prices have continued to push higher, with supply concerns showing little sign of abating. Prices rose on Wednesday, with traders assessing the potential impact of fighting between Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on supply.

item.title: Trump campaigns in Alaska, a conservative state feeling the pinch of high energy prices
item.description: With three weeks until the US midterm elections, Donald Trump on Tuesday campaigned in remote Alaska, one of several conservative states where Democrats have a rare chance of flipping a Senate seat amid voter dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: With three weeks until the US midterm elections , Donald Trump on Tuesday campaigned in remote Alaska, one of several conservative states where Democrats have a rare chance of flipping a Senate seat amid voter dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the Iran war. Polling has shown Democratic candidate Mary Peltola tied or slightly ahead of incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in a state the president carried by some 14 percentage points in 2024. Here, as in much of the United States, the president's approval rating is underwater, hit by rising [USN:L6N45L18J TEXT:"diesel and gasoline prices"] and a conflict in the Middle East that has proven deeply unpopular with voters. Energy shocks have an outsize impact on this vast Arctic state, where people depend on heating oil to brave the long winters and many products must be flown, shipped or trucked across vast distances. Opening for Trump , Sullivan acknowledged that Alaskans face "challenges" when it comes to energy costs. But "the conflict in the Middle East is temporary," he said. "The true forever war is the national Democrats' war against Alaska oil and gas and our jobs." Republicans' decision to hold a rally in Wasilla, a deeply conservative town of roughly 10,000 people about 45 minutes north of Anchorage, the state's most populous city, fits an emerging pattern. The president has taken to [USN:L1N45X06G TEXT:"campaigning"] in conservative-leaning parts of competitive states, rather than in more politically diverse areas with more votes potentially up for grabs. The strategy could help turn out his most devoted supporters on election day, analysts say, while keeping Trump far from the independents and political moderates who have soured on his presidency. Soon after taking the stage at a sports complex surrounded by birch, spruce and aspen trees, Trump vowed the Iran war will "end very soon ... and prices will come tumbling down." "I've done more for this state than any other state in the union," the president said, highlighting his administration's efforts to [USN:S0N44100I TEXT:"attract Asian investment"] in an Alaskan pipeline project, fund new power lines and expand high-speed internet access. At one point, Trump pardoned two local repair shop owners who were convicted of violating the federal Clean Air Act for removing pollution controls on diesel engines. He also encouraged Republicans to vote by mail – a process he has repeatedly sought to [USN:L1N44T0X8 TEXT:"curtail"] and [USN:L6N45718O TEXT:"discredit."] Lance Million, 68, a retired foreman from Wasilla who showed up early to Tuesday's rally, expressed dissatisfaction with the Iran war but said he would vote for Sullivan because, "I’m a Republican, a staunch Republican." “I’m a little bit disappointed in Trump for not getting it (the war in Iran) over with in a timely manner," Million said. Still, he said, "we just don’t have any other choice at this point in time because it’s either Sullivan or Peltola.” POLLS LEAN TOWARD DEMOCRATS All 435 seats in the US House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 US Senate seats will be decided on November 3. Public opinion polls suggest Republicans may [USN:L6N45T19V TEXT:"lose control"] of one or both houses of Congress, which would likely limit Trump's ability to enact his policies in the final two years of his presidency. A New York Times/Siena survey released on October 3 showed Peltola, an Alaska Native who served as the state's sole US House representative from 2022 to 2025, leading by 7 percentage points, though some polls point to a much tighter race. Suzanne Downing, the former communications director for the Alaska Republican Party, said fuel prices were weighing on every aspect of rural life and proving a major drag on Republicans. She said Alaskan men in particular were apathetic about voting this cycle - a potential problem for Republicans as they tend conservative. "They like Trump, but they feel like they've been let down," said Downing. Campaigning in Wasilla could help the president "reinvigorate" his base, she added. Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general, has been a strong advocate for oil and gas drilling, including in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, and has emphasized the state's strategic importance amid growing US competition with Russia and China over control of the Arctic. Peltola made history in 2022 by becoming the first Alaska Native and first woman elected to represent the state in the House of Representatives. She cultivated a pragmatic, bipartisan image and focused on local issues such as fisheries, but lost her 2024 reelection bid to Republican Nick Begich III. Responding to previous criticism from Sullivan over her record, Peltola has said she supports oil and gas development in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and that she is not a typical national Democrat. Jo Bennett, a retired state worker from Anchorage in her 60s who said she has voted for both parties, was among a group of women on Tuesday afternoon putting up placards on an overpass over the highway between Anchorage and Wasilla. Together they read: “War is a pain in the ga$." At a gas station recently, Bennett said, "I about fell over because it was almost $50 to fill my little, pretty-decent-gas-mileage car."

item.title: Blackhawks knock off Penguins in Connor Bedard’s season debut
item.description: Teuvo Teravainen scored twice, including the game-winner with 4:18 left, and Roman Kantserov also had two goals to help the host Chicago Blackhawks defeat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-3 on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Teuvo Teravainen scored twice, including the game-winner with 4:18 left, and Roman Kantserov also had two goals to help the host Chicago Blackhawks defeat the Pittsburgh Penguins 5-3 on Tuesday. Captain Connor Bedard had an assist in his season debut to help Chicago win the opener of Pittsburgh's four-game road trip. Sidney Crosby had two goals, Nick Robertson also scored and Erik Karlsson collected two assists for the Penguins. Crosby tied the game at 9:17 of the third period, gathering a rebound in front of the net and maneuvering around Blackhawks goaltender Spencer Knight (24 saves). Teravainen put Chicago ahead for good at 15:42 when his long wrist shot from the left circle just in front of the goal line got past Pittsburgh goalie Sergei Murashov (15 saves). Teravainen assisted on Tyler Bertuzzi's empty-netter with 10 seconds left for a three-point night. Kantserov, a rookie winger, enjoyed the first multi-goal game of his career while scoring for the third time in the past two games. Teravainen opened the scoring for the Blackhawks just 28 seconds into the game. Anton Frondell's forecheck forced a turnover behind the Pittsburgh net, and Frondell passed the puck to a charging Teravainen in the slot. Pittsburgh has yielded a goal less than 30 seconds into the game twice in its past four contests. Crosby tied the game at 6:57 of the first period, netting his first goal of the season on a wrist shot from the right circle off a 2-on-1 with Karlsson. Chicago regained the lead on the power play at 17:50. Bedard collected a Bowen Byram pass and one-timed the puck to Kantserov, who sent a snapshot from the slot past Murashov. Kantserov extended the advantage to 3-1 at 10:32 of the second. Artyom Levshunov weaved down the right side and into the circle and found Kantserov for a tap-in in front of the net. Pittsburgh narrowed the deficit to one goal at 17:51 as Robertson scored on a rebound off a rush. He gathered a loose puck in front of the net and wristed a shot past Knight. The puck slid under the back of the net and out but the goal counted. Bertuzzi had a goal and assist and Frondell added two assists. Bedard missed training camp and Chicago's first six games while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in July. --Field Level Media

item.title: Soccer viewership in US surging since World Cup
item.description: Record ratings for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States have carried over to U.S. viewership of the sport's top leagues since July, according to Nielsen research findings announced Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Record ratings for the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States have carried over to U.S. viewership of the sport's top leagues since July, according to Nielsen research findings announced Tuesday. Nielsen's Fan Insights data showed that the number of U.S. residents identifying as soccer fans increased 13%, from 66.8 million in July 2025 to 75.2 million in July 2026. Over the past five years, soccer fandom in the U.S. has grown 27%, an increase of 16 million fans. Major League Soccer has seen a 28% boost, adding 11.7 million fans. The findings were unveiled Tuesday at the Front Office Sports Tuned In summit. Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the World Cup final on July 19 averaged 66.4 million viewers in the United States, the largest audience for a soccer match in U.S. history and the most viewers for an American television broadcast since Super Bowl LX in February, when the New England Patriots faced the champion Seattle Seahawks. "The FIFA World Cup 2026 has served as a powerful catalyst for soccer's explosive growth across North America," Nielsen global head of sports Seth Ladetsky said in a statement. "Our data shows that fandom is not only reaching record highs, but it is also expanding rapidly among younger, diverse audiences and carrying over into major domestic and international leagues." Audiences for MLS regular-season games shown on Fox and FS1 after the World Cup break rose 55% among men ages 18-34 and 29% among adults ages 18-34 compared with regular-season matches before the tournament. "The journey started when the World Cup was granted -- it didn't start this summer," MLS commissioner Don Garber said onstage at the Tuned In summit. "What we're looking for as a sport is to grow the market. When I came into MLS, there was no market. ... Our first goal was to build a market where we could come in and deliver something for local fans. And we did that over a period of time. ... Now you've got to have the product that people care about. And frankly, that's just about money and development." Audiences for England's Premier League matches on NBC and USA Network, including Spanish-language broadcasts, have risen 30% among U.S. adults ages 18-34, according to Nielsen. Viewership for Spain's LaLiga on ESPN, ESPN2, ABC and ESPN Deportes has risen 42% year over year across English- and Spanish-language broadcasts, including a 60% increase among viewers ages 18-34. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kyle Palmieri nets pair as Islanders keep Canucks reeling
item.description: Kyle Palmieri scored his first two goals since returning from a knee injury, including the tiebreaking tally in the third period, as the New York Islanders edged the visiting Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Kyle Palmieri scored his first two goals since returning from a knee injury, including the tiebreaking tally in the third period, as the New York Islanders edged the visiting Vancouver Canucks 3-2 on Tuesday night. The goals were Palmieri's first since Nov. 18, when he scored 10 days before suffering a season-ending torn left ACL. The multi-goal game was the first for Palmieri since he scored a pair for the Islanders against the St. Louis Blues on Nov. 23, 2024. Mattias Maccelli scored a goal and added an assist, and Matthew Schaefer collected two assists for the Islanders, who have split their first six games. Ilya Sorokin made 24 saves. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored for the Canucks, who have lost the first four games of their six-game Eastern road trip and five straight overall. Leevi Merilainen recorded 35 saves. Palmieri and Maccelli scored 53 seconds apart late in the first period. Matthew Kessel's shot from the blue line glanced off Palmieri's stick and floated over Merilainen's shoulder with 5:03 left in the period. Maccelli, who spent last season with the Toronto Maple Leafs, scored his first goal for the Islanders following a Vancouver turnover. Schaefer intercepted a clearing pass by Canucks defenseman Zeev Buium and dished the puck to Maccelli, who skated into the lower left faceoff circle before beating Merilainen on the stick side at 15:50. Sasson began the Canucks' comeback bid 7:52 into the second period. Arshdeep Bains shoveled a pass beyond Tony DeAngelo to Sasson, who swooped between DeAngelo and Kessel and fired a shot under Sorokin's glove. Palmieri was called for tripping, setting up Boeser's game-tying goal with 1:05 left in the second. Filip Hronek, at the top of the slot, passed to Elias Pettersson, who fed Boeser. The right winger dropped to one knee and fired a shot past Sorokin, who was screened by teammates Adam Pelech and Ryan Pulock as well as Vancouver's Jake DeBrusk. Palmieri redeemed himself by scoring the eventual game-winning goal 5:38 into the third period. Maccelli collected the rebound of Schaefer's shot and passed to Palmieri, who scored from the high slot with Merilainen screened by Buium. --Field Level Media

item.title: SEC media days: Missouri coach standing by Mark Mitchell in eligibility fight
item.description: Missouri head coach Dennis Gates wasn't scheduled to appear at the SEC's preseason media days until Wednesday, but he got his appearance in Birmingham, Ala., changed to Tuesday for a very important reason
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Missouri head coach Dennis Gates wasn't scheduled to appear at the SEC's preseason media days until Wednesday, but he got his appearance in Birmingham, Ala., changed to Tuesday for a very important reason Gates plans to be with Mark Mitchell in court on Wednesday as the star forward attempts to gain a fifth season of NCAA eligibility. "I am used to it. I don't look at it like a problem," Gates said of the Tigers' uncertain roster three weeks away from the start of the new season. "I've never been given a silver spoon. I've always had to do more with less. I've always had to make decisions at the last minute, last second, but also it allows me to show that I'm talented in what I'm doing. "I'm a CEO, not just a basketball coach. I know how to manage people, manage egos, but also manage a locker room." Mitchell was not selected in this summer's NBA draft. At one point he agreed to an Exhibit 10 contract with the Denver Nuggets, but crucially, he did not sign it. Mitchell also attempted to transfer to Kentucky, but he soon changed course once it became clear the SEC's rule against intraconference transfers would stand in the way, as Mitchell did not enter the portal during the appropriate window. That didn't make Gates think twice about singing the praises of Mitchell, who scored 18.3 points per game and shot 38.8% from 3-point range last season. "When we were 0-19, that young man stepped foot on our campus and the last two years we were able to go to the NCAA Tournament," Gates said. "I'll always be there for Mark Mitchell, man, without a doubt. ... It's about stepping foot, lockstep with them every step of the way, so that they can know that they are supported." The Tigers could be in line for a big year. They were selected eighth in the SEC preseason media poll, on the strength of not just Mitchell but five-star freshmen Jason Crowe Jr. and Toni Bryant. Missouri also has former DePaul leading scorer CJ Gunn in the mix, but again, the program is waiting on an eligibility ruling in his case. "I don't want to sign or would sign anybody that distracts or would distract our locker room," Gates said. "So there was no cutting (players to add Mitchell and Gunn). There was no manipulation." --Alabama coach Nate Oats said he "couldn't be more proud" of Aden Holloway after the former five-star prospect went through a pretrial diversion program for drug charges earlier this year. Holloway is serving a five-game suspension to start the season -- three exhibitions and two regular-season games. He was arrested just before the NCAA Tournament for felony drug possession after authorities said they recovered 2.1 pounds of marijuana from his apartment. His charges have been dismissed. "On the Aden front, I addressed it last week, but super proud of him," Oats said. "He's applied himself consistently over the last few months. Did all the work required to get all the charges dropped. Back in the program I couldn't be more proud of a young man of what he's done over the summer and the fall so far." Holloway averaged 16.8 points and 3.8 assists per game and was an all-SEC selection last year. Oats said Amari Allen will take on the role of primary ball-handler while Holloway is out. --Mark Byington relied heavily on transfers in his first two seasons at Vanderbilt -- and he'll have two transfers with SEC experience this season, T.O. Barrett (Missouri) and Sebastian Williams-Adams (Auburn). But Byington was excited to report that the Commodores are projected to be the second-youngest team in the power conferences this season. "(John Calipari has) got the youngest at Arkansas, but we're right behind them," Byington said. "That's something I know he's used to, and we're getting used to it." Byington said he expects to see his group's youth when they're up against opponents rife with fifth-year players. "But I made a decision, in the current state of college basketball, to believe in the guys I promised something to, the guys I recruited," Byington said. "At the same time, I think you're going to see us continue to get better throughout the year." Seven freshmen are listed on Vanderbilt's roster, including four-star recruits Ethan Mgbako, Anthony Brown and Jackson Sheffield. The Commodores were sixth in the preseason media poll, one spot behind Alabama. --Steven Pearl is approximately one year removed from taking over for his father Bruce Pearl, who retired weeks before the 2025-26 season commenced. Auburn narrowly missed out on the NCAA Tournament in Year 1 under the younger Pearl, but at least one of his players can see a difference entering Year 2. "This year, it's his team," guard Kevin Overton said. "He put together the roster, so he can coach us how he wants... More comfortable. But his approach has always been the same. He wants to win games. You know how bad he wants to win." Steven Pearl, who noted that "You don't realize how valuable an offseason is until you finally have one," said it was a boon for his players and his program to run the table in the NIT and lift the trophy in April. "I wouldn't trade it for anything. I'm glad we did it," Pearl said. "I thought it was really important as a first-year head coach to teach our guys a valuable lesson in life. When something doesn't go your way, you can't just quit. You've got to see things through. ... I thought they had a lot of fun those last four games, really competing." --Patience may be thin in Oklahoma for Porter Moser, who was brought back for a sixth season to coach the Sooners with a promise of increased NIL funds. The Sooners have made just one NCAA Tournament in Moser's first five years, and the media poll picked them 12th in the 16-team league. Moser revealed that one of his most famous conference rivals checked in on him in the middle of a rough patch last season: Arkansas' John Calipari. "You can listen to a lot of things," Moser said. "I've known Cal for many years. I respect him so much when he says that. ... Cal is one of those guys that he's a coaching friend, man, to a lot of people, to the ones he knows and ones that he doesn't. Everybody gets a call when things are going great. Cal is one of those guys that will text or call you and check on you when you're not." --Field Level Media

item.title: China's September exports blow past forecasts, imports accelerate
item.description: China's export growth topped forecasts in September, with robust overseas demand helping offset weak consumer spending and easing pressure on policymakers to deliver this year's growth goal.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Zhang, Ellen Zhang, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: China's export growth topped forecasts in September, with robust overseas demand helping offset weak consumer spending and easing pressure on policymakers to deliver this year's growth goal. Resilience in goods exports has for a second year defied pressure from Western countries seeking more balanced trade with China, keeping factories humming and shoring up economic growth against subdued domestic demand and investment. Exports in September soared 36.3% from a year earlier, outstripping August's 25.0% rise and far exceeding expectations for 25.5% growth, customs data showed on Wednesday. September's growth was the fastest since February this year when exports expanded 39.6%. Imports jumped 31.0%, compared with 28.2% growth in August and economists' forecasts of a 24.5% gain. China's trade surplus reached $938.11 billion in the first nine months of the year, putting the manufacturing powerhouse on course to surpass $1 trillion in surplus sooner than last year unless exports slow sharply in the final quarter. For now, such a slowdown appears unlikely. A [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"deal"] with the European Union to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc, announced earlier this month, is likely to weigh on China's booming auto trade over time. But with the trade measures likely being laid out in [USN:L6N45Y0JN TEXT:"December"], exporters may drive up shipments to beat the deadline. President Xi Jinping's September summit with US President Donald Trump in Washington secured an [USN:L1N45F0IM TEXT:"extension"] to their tariff truce and an agreement to [USN:L6N45K03P TEXT:"cut tariffs"] on $30 billion worth of goods from each side. With the global build-out of AI infrastructure showing little sign of slowing, analysts expect demand for Chinese-made technology products, including semiconductors, to remain robust. China's [USN:L1N460014 TEXT:"factory-gate prices"] rose at their fastest pace in more than four years in September, separate data showed, while consumer inflation edged up but lagged forecasts, underscoring an uneven recovery. The strength in exports, however, indicates that policymakers could still bank on moderate policy support to meet China's 4.5% to 5% annual GDP growth target. The Canton Fair, China's largest trade exhibition, will kick off on Thursday for Chinese manufacturers to showcase their wide array of products to foreign buyers. Going forward, risks of curbs on Chinese exports loom as China continues to defend its industrial and monetary policies, which Washington and Brussels blame for Beijing's massive trade surplus. China's central bank last week [USN:L6N45U0ON TEXT:"pushed back"] against criticism of its exchange-rate policy with a lengthy policy statement, arguing that it never pursued competitive depreciation and rejecting claims that China keeps the yuan artificially weak to gain a trade advantage. As exports now serve as a key growth engine, any major hit to the sector could in turn prompt policymakers to step up stimulus measures to address weak domestic demand and the years-long property market downturn.

item.title: IMF says Britain does not need to speed up fiscal consolidation
item.description: The International Monetary Fund is not recommending that Britain speed up its fiscal consolidation to reduce its budget deficit faster, a senior IMF official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: David Milliken
item.content:encoded: The International Monetary Fund is not recommending that Britain speed up its fiscal consolidation to reduce its budget deficit faster, a senior IMF official said on Wednesday. "Our recommendation is 'stay the course'. We are not saying 'accelerate the pace of consolidation'," fiscal affairs director Rodrigo Valdes said during IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, drawing a contrast with other big economies that have little or no plans to reduce borrowing at a time of rising interest rates. The British government, which ran a budget deficit of 4.4% of GDP last year, aims to balance day-to-day non-investment spending with tax revenue by the 2029/30 financial year – but previous governments regularly failed to meet similar goals. Finance minister John Healey, who arrives at the IMF meetings on Wednesday, will deliver his first annual budget on October 28. He faces extra spending demands from higher debt interest costs and pressures to spend more on defence and energy subsidies, as well as rising welfare costs. Asked if Britain should raise taxes or cut other areas of spending to fund defence, Valdes said many European countries faced similar challenges. "In general ... the space for a lot more revenue, it's not easy. It distorts at the end of the day. So the discussion about the social contract behind spending is very, very urgent," he said. British tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product is close to its highest since just after World War Two, although it is lower than in other European countries with more generous public pensions and welfare systems.

item.title: China, North Korea to open long-delayed bridge on Thursday
item.description: The long-delayed New Yalu River Bridge linking China and North Korea will open on Thursday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua said on Wednesday, signalling a renewed push to boost trade despite Pyongyang's lingering wariness of greater economic dependence.
item.dc:creator: Liz Lee, Kyu-Seok Shim
item.content:encoded: The long-delayed New Yalu River Bridge linking China and North Korea will open on Thursday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua said on Wednesday, signalling a renewed push to boost trade despite Pyongyang's lingering wariness of greater economic dependence. The two sides will jointly hold an opening ceremony, the Xinhua report said. North Korea's state media did not immediately report on the plan. The bridge will be the largest and most significant land crossing for trade between the two countries. China completed its side of the bridge in 2014, [USN:L8N45U017 TEXT:"hoping to boost trade ties"], although North Korea left its approach roads and customs facilities unfinished as relations soured over Pyongyang's nuclear tests and the UN sanctions that followed. The opening of the new bridge signals further progress in bilateral relations between Beijing and Pyongyang, weeks after North Korea opened its [USN:L6N44Z0JD TEXT:"first road bridge"] with Russia. The North's ties with Moscow have advanced rapidly since their leaders' meeting in 2023. China's exports to North Korea rose to a six-year high of $2.3 billion last year, a 25% increase over the previous year. That was still well below levels before UN sanctions were tightened in 2017. China and Russia have since questioned the legitimacy of the UN Security Council resolutions that they had voted to pass and have been accused by countries such as South Korea and the US of conducting trade and exchanges in breach of the sanctions. China is by far North Korea's largest trading partner, but the opening of the new bridge carries added significance as the isolated state expands external exchanges after the pandemic amid Pyongyang's efforts to balance relations with its two key economic and strategic partners. North Korea and Russia opened a road bridge last month across the Tumen River, adding another transport link as Pyongyang expands economic and strategic cooperation with Moscow. The 3-km (2-mile) dual-carriageway bridge connects the Chinese border city of Dandong with Sinuiju in North Korea and is intended to replace the ageing, single-lane Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge as the main route for road trade. Cho Han-bum, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification in Seoul, said further putting off the opening could have been a source of unwanted strains for both, even as Pyongyang remains cautious of greater economic dependence on China. “There is always both wariness and cooperation in North Korea-China relations,” he said.

item.title: Australian court dismisses Cosette appeal to drop Mayne Pharma takeover
item.description: Australia's New South Wales Court of Appeal on Wednesday rejected Cosette Pharmaceuticals' bid to terminate its takeover of Mayne Pharma , upholding a lower court ruling that the US-based drugmaker had no valid grounds to abandon the deal.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's New South Wales Court of Appeal on Wednesday rejected Cosette Pharmaceuticals' bid to terminate its takeover of Mayne Pharma (MYX.AX) , upholding a lower court ruling that the US-based drugmaker had no valid grounds to abandon the deal. Here are some of the details: Cosette bid [USN:L1N3WX01N TEXT:"A$7.40 per share"] for Mayne in February last year but later tried to back out, saying a deterioration in Mayne's financial performance constituted a material adverse change that voided the agreement. The NSW Court of Appeal upheld the trial judge's finding that the decline in Mayne's sales performance was insufficient to meet the threshold for a material adverse change under the scheme implementation deed. The appeal court held that through its conduct at the first court hearing on the scheme, Cosette had chosen to affirm the deed, giving up any right it may have had to terminate. The court rejected Cosette's claim that Mayne had misled it regarding its expected 2025 earnings performance. It ordered Cosette to pay the legal costs of the appeal. Mayne Pharma will continue to pursue claims for damages against Cosette, parent Cosette Pharmaceuticals Holdings, and controllers David Burgstahler and Avista Capital on behalf of itself and its shareholders, Mayne Pharma Chair Bruce Robinson said. "Mayne Pharma remains committed to continuing to maximise shareholder value and remains focused on continuing to strengthen the business," Robinson said. The A$672 million ($470.13 million) takeover has faced political opposition, with South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas criticising the transaction. Federal Treasurer Jim Chalmers [USN:L1N3WX01N TEXT:"blocked"] the deal in November last year on national interest grounds. Shares of Mayne Pharma rose as much as 11% to A$2.820, logging their best intraday session in more than two months, after trading resumed. Cosette has until November 11 to appeal the decision in the High Court, Mayne Pharma said. ($1 = 1.4294 Australian dollars)

item.title: Pius Suter, Mason McTavish help Blues wallop Senators 7-2
item.description: Pius Suter and Mason McTavish each had two goals and an assist in the St. Louis Blues' 7-2 win over the host Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pius Suter and Mason McTavish each had two goals and an assist in the St. Louis Blues' 7-2 win over the host Ottawa Senators on Tuesday night. Jake Neighbours scored twice and rookie defenseman Adam Jiricek got his first career goal in his sixth game for the Blues, who won their second straight. Pavel Buchnevich had three assists, Connor McMichael added two assists and Joel Hofer made 15 saves. Claude Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund scored for the Senators in their second of back-to-back games and third in four nights. Samuel Ersson stopped 19 shots. Suter's short-handed goal with 5:32 left in the first period gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead. He went in on a partial breakaway after taking a pass from defenseman Colton Parayko for the sixth short-handed goal of Suter's career. Neighbours made it 2-0 with 6:40 remaining in the second when he beat Ersson from above the high slot. Giroux closed the gap to 2-1 with 2:08 left in the middle period when he connected from the top portion of the right circle. It was thanks to an outstanding effort from Tim Stutzle to get a free puck at the left of the net and then pass to Giroux, who tied Hall of Famer Bobby Hull for 59th all-time with 1,170 points. But McTavish restored the two-goal margin 33 seconds later when he capped a 3-on-2 rush by backhanding the puck into an open net from the top of the crease. Suter's second goal 7:54 into the third period made it 4-1, when his harmless-looking shot from just above the goal line in the left corner went into the short side off Ersson. Neighbours got his second goal with 5:14 left by slamming Buchnevich's pass across the top of the crease into the open side of the net. McTavish's second tally and Jiricek's goal came in the final five minutes. Zetterlund picked up a power-play goal for Ottawa with 1:27 left. Senators defenseman Nikolas Matinpalo was out after suffering an upper-body injury Monday. Ottawa continued to be without top-four defensemen Jake Sanderson (lower body) and Artem Zub (knee). --Field Level Media

item.title: Kraken top Flyers in shootout; Philadelphia winless in first eight
item.description: Bobby McMann scored in regulation and then netted the decisive goal in the shootout as the visiting Seattle Kraken nipped the winless Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Bobby McMann scored in regulation and then netted the decisive goal in the shootout as the visiting Seattle Kraken nipped the winless Philadelphia Flyers 3-2 on Tuesday. Ville Ottavainen scored the other regulation goal for the Kraken, who improved to 3-0-0 on their five-game road trip. Seattle goaltender Philipp Grubauer made 24 saves through overtime and then stopped four of five attempts in the shootout. Philadelphia dropped to 0-5-3 on the season, continuing the longest winless start to a campaign in team history. Christian Dvorak and Trevor Zegras scored a goal apiece while Dan Vladar finished with 29 saves and notched an assist. After Grubauer stopped Zegras to open the shootout, Matty Beniers snapped a shot five-hole through Vladar. Matvei Michkov countered with a goal following a series of moves near the crease. That would be the last goal until the fifth round, when McMann placed a perfect shot into the top-left corner to end it. The Flyers trailed 2-0 after two periods before scoring two goals in 1:13 early in the third. Dvorak got them on the board at 6:07 with a goal off a feed from rookie defenseman Oliver Bonk. Zegras got them even at 7:20 as he converted a Travis Sanheim setup for his first goal of the season. In overtime, Philadelphia was whistled for too many men on the ice with 2:39 remaining. The Kraken controlled the action for most of the man advantage but were unable to pot a game-winner. Seattle took a 1-0 lead 7:57 into the contest on McMann's power-play goal. It doubled the lead 8:54 into the second period on Ottavainen's shot through traffic. Zegras was whistled for two penalties in the second period, both involving scrums with Grubauer after the whistle. At one point in that stretch, Seattle had a 5-on-3 for 38 seconds, although Philadelphia's defense held firm, setting the stage for the third-period comeback. --Field Level Media

item.title: Indian shares muted as oil prices, foreign outflows offset IT rebound
item.description: Indian shares were little changed in morning trade on Wednesday as a rebound paused, with rising oil prices and sustained foreign outflows weighing on sentiment while investors assess corporate earnings.
item.dc:creator: Bharath Rajeswaran
item.content:encoded: Indian shares were little changed in morning trade on Wednesday as a rebound paused, with rising oil prices and sustained foreign outflows weighing on sentiment while investors assess corporate earnings. The Nifty 50 (.NSEI) added 0.07% to 22,738.05, while the BSE Sensex (.BSESN) edged 0.13% higher to 73,128.50 as of 09:46 a.m. IST. They swung between 0.2% gains and 0.2% losses in morning trade. Eight of the 16 major sectors logged losses. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100) and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100) were little changed. IT index (.NIFTYIT) , which gained 5.2% in the previous session, added 1.2% on the day. Both the Nifty and Sensex (.BSESN) climbed about 1.6% on [USN:L4N45Z0KR TEXT:"Tuesday"], led by information technology stocks after HCLTech's (HCLT.NS) [USN:L6N45Z08A TEXT:"quarterly profit"] beat expectations.
