item.title: Six deaths confirmed in Florida from Hurricane Isaias, governor says
item.description: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said on Tuesday six people had been confirmed dead in the state from Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall last week.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said on Tuesday six people had been confirmed dead in the state from [USN:L6N45W00A TEXT:"Hurricane Isaias"], which made landfall last week. "We have now had six storm-related fatalities," DeSantis told reporters The six deaths included two that had been previously confirmed. Those two deaths were in Escambia County in the state's far west. One person died when a tree fell on their home while the other died from carbon monoxide exposure caused by a generator operating inside their garage, officials said DeSantis said the four newly confirmed deaths included a car crash at an intersection where the traffic signal was not working and storm-related disruptions to the medical treatment of two people Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday and left hundreds of thousands of residents in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi without power Alabama Governor Kay Ivey said on Saturday that two people had died as a result of the storm in her state

item.title: Alexis Lafreniere scores twice, Rangers beat Lightning to stay unbeaten at home
item.description: Alexis Lafreniere scored twice in the first period to continue his hot start as the New York Rangers remained unbeaten on home ice with a 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alexis Lafreniere scored twice in the first period to continue his hot start as the New York Rangers remained unbeaten on home ice with a 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning on Tuesday night. Tye Kartye set up both Lafreniere goals after scoring twice in Sunday's 6-2 rout of the Vancouver Canucks. Mika Zibanejad also scored unassisted on a short-handed, empty-net goal with 2:44 remaining during the final seconds of Tampa Bay's 6-on-4 power play. Lafreniere scored his sixth and seventh goals in the opening 12:47 as the Rangers improved to 5-0-0 at home. It is New York's best start on home ice since opening the 1990-91 season with eight straight victories and third time in team history that the Rangers won their first five home games. Lafreniere also scored for a career-high fourth straight game and notched his 12th career multi-goal game to continue his strong start after getting his seventh goal in his 31st game last season. Will Cuylle scored late in the second period for the Rangers, who won for the sixth time in eight games and beat Tampa Bay for the second time after pulling away for a 5-1 victory over the visiting Lightning on Oct. 1. Dylan Garand made 25 saves in New York's second game since losing star goalie Igor Shesterkin to a season-ending lower-body injury. He improved his career record to 5-1-1 and highlighted the win with a point-blank glove save on John Carlson with 8:16 remaining. Garand also made a pad save on Brayden Point's backhand try with about 5 1/2 minutes left and another stop on Nikita Kucherov with 3 1/2 minutes left during Tampa Bay's 6-on-4 power play. Zemgus Girgensons scored late in the opening period for the Lightning, whose four-game winning streak was stopped. Tampa Bay goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy made 19 saves. Lafreniere opened the scoring 62 seconds into the contest when he went to the front of the net, withstood a scramble, took a pass from Kartye and chipped the puck into the net. He scored shortly after Kartye knocked Tampa Bay defenseman Victor Hedman off the puck in the right corner. Lafreniere made it 2-0 at 12:47 by fending off Anthony Cirelli and finishing off a breakaway when Kartye made a long backhand pass while clearing the defensive zone. Girgensons put a shot by Garand from the left circle with 2:34 left in the opening period. Cuylle re-directed a shot from Sean Durzi past Vasilevskiy with 94 seconds left in the second period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vietnam says trade talks with US nearly completed; US officials more cautious
item.description: Vietnam and the US have nearly completed negotiations covering a trade deal, Vietnamese Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc said on Wednesday at an event in Hanoi, though US officials appeared more cautious.
item.dc:creator: Khanh Vu, Francesco Guarascio
item.content:encoded: Vietnam and the US have nearly completed negotiations covering a trade deal, Vietnamese Deputy Prime Minister Pham Gia Tuc said on Wednesday at an event in Hanoi, though US officials appeared more cautious. Export-reliant Vietnam has been in talks for more than a year with the US, its main foreign market, to avoid punitive tariffs. Trump administration officials have repeatedly accused the country of being used as a transit point to lower duties on Chinese goods bound for the US. Vietnam has sent the final text of the agreement to the US, Tuc said at a business forum in Hanoi. "We expect the US to continue to create favorable conditions for Vietnamese goods to access the US market in a stable and sustainable manner," Tuc said. After the US' global tariffs were struck down by the Supreme Court in February, the Trump administration launched three investigations into Vietnam's trade practices. One covering alleged failures to prevent the use of goods made with forced labour ended with 12.5% tariffs on Vietnamese products, higher than most of its regional peers. The other two investigations covering industrial overcapacity and the protection of intellectual property rights are underway and could result in additional tariffs. Tuc said Vietnam expects the US to make objective and balanced assessments in these investigations. Top Vietnamese leader To Lam has been invited by the US to attend the G20 summit in Florida in December, Vietnamese state media reported, raising hopes that a deal could be sealed then. US CAUTIOUS David Fogel, the US assistant secretary of commerce, in a recorded message streamed at the event, said he was “hopeful” the two countries would continue to work together on a trade agreement. He warned that the US' deficit with Vietnam was the largest that the US has with any partner. Vietnam's trade surplus with the US exceeded $163 billion in the January-to-August period, greater than the US' bigger trading partners like Mexico and China, according to the latest US trade data. Among options to balance trade flows, Fogel urged Vietnamese businesses to invest more in the US and noted the US could export "world-class super-intelligence hardware" to Vietnam. The country currently faces restrictions over its access to the US' most advanced technologies. Jennifer Wicks, the US ambassador to Vietnam, reiterated at the event that talks on a trade deal were ongoing. She urged Vietnam to adapt its regulatory framework on data protection to attract investment and allow businesses to deploy new technologies efficiently. US tech companies have [USN:L6N3MA013 TEXT:"repeatedly warned"] that Vietnam’s strict limits on cross-border data transfers discourage investment in the country. Wicks also urged Vietnam to develop predictable policies and stable rules on pricing to favour foreign investment in its expanding energy sector. Vietnam has been negotiating for years with potential foreign investors on prices that it would pay for electricity generated by power plants. It has also retroactively cut price subsidies for some investors in renewables.

item.title: IMF dials up calls for urgent fiscal consolidation
item.description: The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday issued an urgent call for advanced economies and others to reduce government spending, cut deficits and lower debt levels, warning that delays would only make the job harder in coming years.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The International Monetary Fund on Wednesday issued an urgent call for advanced economies and others to reduce government spending, cut deficits and lower debt levels, warning that delays would only make the job harder in coming years. Rodrigo Valdes, head of the IMF's Fiscal Affairs department, said rising sovereign bond yields were adding to fiscal pressures at a time when average public debt was poised to hit 100% of gross domestic product, the highest seen since World War Two, leaving countries with less margin for delay. "We're saying now it's urgent and it's now because basically the conditions have changed," Valdes said, noting the risks posed by inflationary pressures, high levels of global debt and rising sovereign bond yields. "So, if you want one message, we dialed up the urgency of our message." Ahead of this week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok, Valdes had told Reuters that "the fiscal results this year are worse than expected six months ago, and worse than they were one year ago." The majority of countries were now looking at boosting spending instead of tightening their belts, he said. NEED TO BUILD POLITICAL SUPPORT Valdes said the challenge for major advanced economies with high debt levels was to build political support for concrete plans to contain borrowing costs in the medium term, and limit spillovers to the rest of the world. "The more countries wait, the more painful the adjustment becomes," the IMF said in a blog released on Wednesday . Delaying adjustments would lead to increasing interest burdens and fiscal vulnerabilities, further narrowing policy options. Financing conditions for many emerging market and developing economies had remained favorable, but might not last, the IMF said, urging those countries to also reduce their fiscal vulnerabilities and strengthen debt management. Low-income countries, where external financing was already tighter, needed to strengthen their tax systems and improve spending efficiency, the IMF said. High oil prices, persistent inflation, stronger investment demand and higher-than-expected AI growth have driven sharp increases in long-term sovereign yields in recent months. The Group of Seven's average 10-year government bond yield rose over 110 basis points between February and September, reaching its highest level in nearly two decades, the IMF said. The IMF said the effective average cost of government financing was projected to rise to 3.7% by 2031 from 2.3% in 2021. In the US, interest payments were expected to reach 5.3% of GDP, up from 2.8% of GDP before the COVID pandemic, roughly equal to its projected expenditure on Social Security. That number was even higher in low-income countries, where interest payments today consume over 15% of tax revenues, compared to an average cost of around 9% between 2011 and 2019. Adding to the stress, governments in advanced economies were refinancing more debt at shorter maturities, causing higher rates to pass through to government costs more quickly, the IMF said. For the G7 and Spain, it said, the share of debt maturing within one year was now approaching 30%. Inflation rates above target and higher energy prices meant central bankers would likely need to keep rates higher for longer, which in turn would limit governments' ability to respond to downturns, just as demands for increased spending on defense, energy security and aging populations were mounting. The IMF said interest rates on debt also now exceeded expected nominal growth rates in a number of countries, which would make it even harder for them to stabilize debt. Valdes said more countries were allowing higher energy prices to pass through, but many were still relying on costly, broad-based measures to shield their populations. "Our estimate is that taken together, the fiscal cost of all these measures is about one half percent of global GDP (gross domestic product)," he said, noting that a continuation of such measures would drive prices higher at the global level.

item.title: SK Group Chairman Chey sells stake to Dell family office fund for $406 million
item.description: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million), a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won has agreed the sale of a 1.34% stake in holding company SK Inc (034730.KS) to an investment fund linked to Dell Technologies (DELL.N) founder Michael Dell for 544 billion won ($406 million), a regulatory filing showed on Wednesday. The deal is part of Chey's plan to raise 944 billion won through share sales to pay a divorce settlement to his former wife. Here are some details: The buyer of 972,493 SK Inc shares was identified as DFO Public Investments, L.P., a Delaware-based investment fund affiliated with DFO Management, the family investment office of Michael Dell, according to the filing and DFO Management's website. Earlier this month, SK Inc said in a filing that Chey had agreed to [USN:L1N45O06F TEXT:"sell 1.65 million shares, or a 2.26% stake"] for 944 billion won. Of those, 681,431 shares, or 0.94%, will be sold to Korea Investment & Securities for 400 billion won. SK had previously identified the buyer of the remaining shares only as a strategic investor, saying the investor had agreed to buy the stake after considering SK Inc's business competitiveness and medium- to long-term growth prospects. Dell Technologies, a major supplier of AI servers and data centre infrastructure, has business ties with SK Hynix (000660.KS) , SK Group's memory chipmaking unit. The stake is being acquired by a Dell family investment fund, rather than Dell Technologies itself. Reuters reported in May that global technology companies had approached SK Hynix with [USN:L4N41K05W TEXT:"proposals"] to invest in dedicated memory chip production lines and help finance costly manufacturing equipment as they sought to secure supplies amid booming AI demand. The Korea Corporate Governance Forum said Chey and the buyers would be required to disclose their stakes as joint holdings if they had agreed, even informally, to exercise their voting rights in the same way. Failure to do so would violate South Korea's capital markets law, it said. The forum, an independent watchdog that monitors corporate governance issues in South Korea, said a strategic investor suggested their interests could be aligned, raising the possibility that the fund could be deemed a joint holder with Chey under the law. ($1 = 1,339.6000 won)

item.title: Andrei Svechnikov, Canes take down Caps for sixth straight win
item.description: Andrei Svechnikov's second goal of the game lifted the Carolina Hurricanes to their sixth consecutive victory by beating the Washington Capitals 4-2 on Tuesday night in Raleigh, N.C.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Andrei Svechnikov's second goal of the game lifted the Carolina Hurricanes to their sixth consecutive victory by beating the Washington Capitals 4-2 on Tuesday night in Raleigh, N.C. Svechnikov, who also had an assist, gave the Hurricanes their first lead with 6:04 remaining with a power-play tally. Carolina had been 0-for-4 on power plays until that sequence. Eric Robinson and Mark Jankowski, whose empty-net goal came with 1:27 remaining, also scored for the Hurricanes, who avenged a 5-2 loss to the Capitals in the same arena less than two weeks earlier. Sebastian Aho posted two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov made 20 saves. Boone Jenner and Justin Holl had Washington's goals, and Ryan Leonard provided two assists. Logan Thompson stopped 31 shots, but the Capitals lost their second straight game. Svechnikov has compiled six goals and five assists in the season's first eight games. The Hurricanes revealed earlier in the day that captain Jordan Staal will miss at least a month with a calf injury. Jenner opened the scoring with the only first-period goal. Svechnikov put Carolina on the board 3:58 into the second period. Holl and Robinson scored later in the period for a 2-2 tie. Jankowski's goal enabled him to extend the best opening stretch of his career with his fifth goal this month. Hurricanes forward Taylor Hall played less than 4 1/2 minutes as he exited with an upper-body injury, according to TSN.ca. It was the beginning of Capitals star Alex Ovechkin's farewell tour since he announced last week this would be his final season. This marked the final regular-season game in Raleigh for the Capitals, who selected the winger in the 2004 NHL Draft that was held in the same building where Tuesday night's game was played. Ovechkin had two shots on goal in 13 minutes of ice time. Washington didn't convert on its two power plays. --Field Level Media

item.title: Asia shares edge up as chip selloff eases; US CPI awaited
item.description: Asian shares inched higher on Wednesday as those related to artificial intelligence found respite after a selloff, while any gain was tempered by elevated oil prices and caution ahead of U.S. inflation data later in the global day.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxing Li
item.content:encoded: Asian shares inched higher on Wednesday as those related to artificial intelligence found respite after a selloff, while any gain was tempered by elevated oil prices and caution ahead of U.S. inflation data later in the global day. Among firms in the AI supply chain, chipmakers Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK Hynix (000660.KS) rose more than 2% in South Korea while Kioxia (285A.T) was steady in Japan, recovering some of the [USN:L6N45Z12J TEXT:"previous session's loss"]. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) was up 0.5% after U.S. stocks ended the previous session with a mild loss. Japan's Nikkei (.N225) rose 0.2% and South Korea's Kospi (.KS11) added 1.8%. Sentiment remained cautious, however, with oil prices elevated as concern over energy supplies intensified following Houthi missile and drone attacks on [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"]. U.S. crude ticked up 0.8% to $94.96 a barrel. Brent crude rose to $106.6. "After yesterday's chip-led sell-off in the region ... market participants will be gauging whether shakiness across major indices eases. The geopolitical situation globally and the impact on energy markets won't help," said analyst Kyle Rodda at Capital.com. In another sign of risk aversion, longer-dated bonds rallied as investors sought safety. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was steady at 5.221% after touching its lowest in nearly two weeks, while that on 30-year notes held at 5.569% following a three-day decline. On Wall Street overnight, U.S. bank stocks lost ground after [USN:L1N45Z0O3 TEXT:"mixed quarterly earnings results"] from Citigroup (C.N) and peers, weighing on broader markets. U.S. stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis , were up 0.04% at 7,858.8. CPI TEST AWAITED Market participants were awaiting US consumer price index data (USCPF=ECI) on Wednesday, hoping to extract clues on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook. On average, economists estimated headline inflation accelerated to an annual 3.6% in September due to rebounding energy prices, with the core CPI rising 0.2% on a monthly basis. "The risk is the core CPI surprises to the upside because of strong consumer demand and higher costs, pushing up market pricing of an October Fed hike and the USD," said currency strategist Carol Kong at Commonwealth Bank of Australia. Investors priced in a 22% chance of an October interest rate hike ahead of the CPI data, the CME FedWatch Tool showed. New York Federal Reserve President John Williams [USN:L6N45Z14X TEXT:"said"] the Fed may need to raise its policy rate once more this year to slow inflation, but that he sees no need for hikes in 2027. The dollar index , which tracks the greenback against the currencies of some major trading partners, was down at 102.17. The euro was little changed at $1.1202. Market participants were also awaiting Chinese inflation data on Wednesday, looking for signs of reviving domestic demand amid deflationary pressure.

item.title: Canadiens relinquish two-goal lead, sink Sabres in shootout
item.description: Cole Caufield and Lane Hutson each had a goal and an assist and the Montreal Canadiens recovered for a 4-3 shootout win against the visiting Buffalo Sabres on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Cole Caufield and Lane Hutson each had a goal and an assist and the Montreal Canadiens recovered for a 4-3 shootout win against the visiting Buffalo Sabres on Tuesday. Alexandre Texier scored the deciding goal in the shootout, Juraj Slafkovsky had two assists and Jacob Fowler made 14 saves for the Canadiens, who have won two straight games via the shootout. Olen Zellweger scored twice and Mattias Samuelsson and Beck Malenstyn each had two assists for the Sabres, who have lost three of their last four. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 35 saves. Trailing 3-1, Buffalo scored twice in the span of a minute early in the third period to tie it. Josh Norris pulled his team within one at 4:24, firing a shot from the middle of the blue line that went off Montreal defenseman Adam Engstrom past Fowler on the glove side. Zellweger's second of the night tied it 3-3 at 5:25, taking a pass from Zach Benson at the left point and sending through traffic to beat Fowler blocker side. After the scoreless overtime period, Caufield, Texier and Zachary Bolduc scored for the Canadiens in the shootout, while Tage Thompson found the net for the Sabres. Zellweger gave Buffalo a 1-0 lead at 2:16 of the first period. He took a feed from Samuelsson at the left point and fired a snap shot through traffic that deflected off Engstrom's and redirected past Fowler. Hutson capitalized in the final seconds of a 5-on-3 power play to tie it. Slafkovsky returned a pass to Hutson, who then snapped it from above the right circle to beat a screened Luukkonen at 14:28, with eight seconds remaining in the two-man advantage. Caufield put the hosts ahead 2-1 off the rush at 1:19 of the second period. Slafkovsky took a short drop pass from Nick Suzuki along the right side and dished it to Caufield in the left circle, where he quickly fired it past Luukkonen's right arm. The Canadiens took advantage of the Sabres' inability to clear the zone to make it 3-1. Hutson intercepted a rim up the wall by the visitors, passed it to Bolduc who returned it to him, and Hutson fed Josh Anderson for a one-timer that went bar down on Luukkonen at 19:10 of the second period. --Field Level Media

item.title: China factory-gate inflation heats up as commodity costs rise, CPI lags forecasts
item.description: China's producer prices rose at their fastest pace in more than four years in September while consumer inflation edged up, as pricier oil and commodities lifted factory-gate costs even as weak domestic demand kept broader price pressures contained.
item.dc:creator: Qiaoyi Li, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: China's producer prices rose at their fastest pace in more than four years in September while consumer inflation edged up, as pricier oil and commodities lifted factory-gate costs even as weak domestic demand kept broader price pressures contained. The data suggests prices are revving up for manufacturers, but weak consumer demand continues to restrain inflation, reinforcing concerns that China still faces an uneven recovery driven more by exports than spending. Household spending remains subdued and private-sector confidence fragile despite a series of stimulus measures, underscoring persistent weakness in domestic demand and broader economic imbalances. The producer price index rose 5% from a year earlier, National Bureau of Statistics data showed on Wednesday, up from 3.8% in August and beating the estimated 4.5% rise in a Reuters poll. That marks the fastest pace of factory-gate inflation since June 2022. "Much of the upward pressure still came from commodity supply disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, with prices rising particularly sharply in fuel processing, chemicals and non-ferrous metals," said Nguyen Hoang Nam, China economist at Capital Economics, who expects prices to fall back next year. Higher oil and commodity prices, driven by transport disruptions, adverse weather and geopolitical tensions, have increased cost pressures for manufacturers, though sluggish demand has limited the pass-through to consumers. The consumer price index (CPI) gained 0.9% year-on-year, compared with a 0.8% increase in August, and came in below economists' forecast for a 1% rise. Gasoline prices soared 16.6% from a year earlier and contributed about 0.47 percentage points to headline CPI growth, the statistics agency said. Underlying consumer price pressures, however, remained muted, suggesting households are still cautious about spending. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, was up 1% on the year, unchanged from August. Zhou Hao, chief economist at Guotai Junan International, said a key question is whether stronger industrial momentum can gradually feed into employment, income growth and consumer confidence. "If that transmission mechanism improves, the current divergence between producer and consumer prices could narrow from the demand side, creating a more balanced and durable recovery in 2027." Markets were little changed, with China's blue-chip index (.CSI300) down 0.1% and the Shanghai Composite (.SSEC) up 0.1%. Beijing has stepped up support for the economy, [USN:L6N45V0EV TEXT:"approving"] an additional 550 billion yuan ($82.15 billion) in unused local government bond quota for infrastructure and other spending, adding to [USN:L1N45L0BK TEXT:"measures"] such as mortgage subsidies. Month-on-month, CPI ticked up 0.2%, versus expectations for a 0.3% gain and a 0.4% increase in August. ($1 = 6.6953 Chinese yuan)

item.title: Tkachuk brothers make NHL history as Panthers top Blue Jackets
item.description: Brady Tkachuk recorded a natural hat trick during an 8:03 span of the second period, brother Matthew Tkachuk posted five assists and the visiting Florida Panthers won 7-3 over the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brady Tkachuk recorded a natural hat trick during an 8:03 span of the second period, brother Matthew Tkachuk posted five assists and the visiting Florida Panthers won 7-3 over the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday night. Matthew assisted on all three of Brady's goals, making him the first to assist on each of a brother's natural hat trick, according to the NHL. Brady Tkachuk added one assist for four points; the point totals tied a career high for each Tkachuk. Seth Jones had four assists, Carter Verhaeghe scored twice and Sam Reinhart posted two goals with a helper for Florida, which went 4-for-6 on the power play. With Jacob Markstrom day-to-day due to tightness, Florida's Akira Schmid made 24 saves. Kent Johnson scored early, while Denton Mateychuk and Cole Sillinger each added a late goal for the Blue Jackets. Cam Talbot stopped 17 of 23 shots before being pulled in the third period for Columbus. Johnson opened the scoring with 5:49 remaining in the first period. Off an own-zone Panthers turnover, Johnson possessed the puck, broke free and went low to beat Schmid. Florida, though, tied it 2:27 into the second period, when Matthew Tkachuk slid the puck through the slot for Brady to record his first goal as a Panther. Less than four minutes later, and on the power play, a circle-stationed Matthew sent the puck into the slot for Brady to bury. Tkachuk completed the natural hat trick with 9:30 left in the middle frame. Again on the power play, Brady benefited from a generous bounce off the end-board of Reinhart's shot for a top-shelf conversion. With 6:16 to go in the second, Columbus' Mathieu Olivier was issued a five-minute major penalty and game misconduct for his slash between the legs of Florida's Uvis Balinskis. And, in the waning moments of that extended power play with 2:10 remaining before the second intermission, the Tkachuk brothers set up Verhaeghe's successful net-side one-timer. Matthew Tkachuk's fifth assist came 1:20 into the third, via Reinhart's tip-in, power-play score. Verhaeghe's wrister through traffic with 16:32 remaining in regulation made it 6-1 and ended Talbot's night. Columbus' Jet Greaves stopped all four shots faced in relief. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil prices climb as Iran deploys new tactics to target ships transiting Hormuz
item.description: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying new tactics to target ships, as Tehran seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Yuka Obayashi, Emily Chow
item.content:encoded: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after two vessels [USN:L1N45Z0YL TEXT:"were struck"] in the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian officials told Reuters they were deploying [USN:L8N45Z15J TEXT:"new tactics"] to target ships, as Tehran seeks to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections. Brent crude futures rose 63 cents, or 0.6%, to $106.32 a barrel by 0345 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures gained 66 cents, or 0.7%, to $94.80 a barrel. Both contracts rose more than $1 in earlier trade before paring some gains. The Iranian officials declined to provide details of the new strategy, but one said that Iran had started using different offensive tactics against vessels it considered in violation of its restrictions about 10 days ago, adding that this had led to an increase in attacks on such ships. A container ship and a tanker were hit by unknown projectiles within the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. "The fact that Iranian officials are openly admitting to undermining US efforts to keep oil prices under control speaks volumes about the real intentions behind the so-called 'peace talks,'" said Priyanka Sachdeva, head of market insights at Phillip Nova. "Iran is well aware of its geographical importance and the havoc higher oil prices can inflict on the global economy, and it may not shy away from using this leverage." Elsewhere, the Iran-allied Houthis [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"attacked"] an administrative building belonging to state-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) in the city of Dhahran, causing a limited fire, Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Wednesday. The group has fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia over the past week in retaliation for the kingdom's support of Yemeni government forces. Riyadh's [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"international airport"] has been hit four times, with a strike on Saturday killing 13 people. "Supply concern stemming from conflict between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia is driving prices higher," said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist at Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities. "However, the expectation that increased Russian diesel exports will ease market tightness is likely to limit sharp price movement in either direction," Kikukawa said, projecting WTI to trade between $90 and $100 a barrel. Last month, Saudi Arabia raised oil production despite disruptions to shipments caused by the US-Iran war. That led to a [USN:L6N45Z0RG TEXT:"sharp production increase"] from OPEC+ — the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and partners including Russia — OPEC said on Tuesday. In Russia, the government said on Tuesday it [USN:L1N45Z0B7 TEXT:"did not see"] any direct link between peace talks with Ukraine and its deal to [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"export diesel"] to the US. The comment came after Reuters reported that US envoys had told Ukrainian officials on Friday that the deal was part of an attempt to draw Russia back to negotiations for a [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"peace settlement"].

item.title: India boat capsizes, drowning 13, mostly children
item.description: A boat capsized in India's eastern state of Bihar, drowning 13 people, most of them children, police said, while six aboard were rescued.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A boat capsized in India's eastern state of Bihar, drowning 13 people, most of them children, police said, while six aboard were rescued. The boat overturned on Tuesday in the state's central district of Vaishali, while carrying passengers to a feast in a neighbouring village, district magistrate Varsha Singh told media. Police are investigating the cause of the incident, regional police officer Subodh Kumar told Reuters on Wednesday, giving the tally of those rescued.

item.title: Dollar languishes as focus turns to CPI, Fed speakers
item.description: The dollar languished on Wednesday as traders awaited fresh signals on the timing for interest rate hikes to contend with persistent inflation.
item.dc:creator: Rocky Swift
item.content:encoded: The dollar languished on Wednesday as traders awaited fresh signals on the timing for interest rate hikes to contend with persistent inflation. The greenback weakened from an 18-month high in the previous session as oil prices eased and investors reassessed the AI-fueled rally that has supported demand for US assets. The euro clung to gains as budget concerns in France kept regional bond yields elevated and markets on edge. Attention now focuses on the release of US consumer price index data as well as speeches from Federal Reserve policymakers that could clarify the outlook for interest rates. "The risk is the core CPI surprises to the upside because of strong consumer demand and higher costs, pushing up market pricing of an October Fed hike and the USD," Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said in a note. The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, edged 0.02% lower to 102.16, following a 0.35% slide on Tuesday. The euro rose 0.04% at $1.1203. The yen was little changed at 158.32 per dollar, and sterling rose 0.03% to $1.3256. The dollar extended losses on Tuesday after New York Fed President John Williams said [USN:FWN45Z0WW TEXT:"he still expects"] one more rate hike this year, but sees no need for further increases in 2027. The US Labor Department is due to release its CPI for September, which is expected to have risen 0.6% month-on-month after increasing 0.4% in August, while annual inflation is seen accelerating to 3.6% from 3.4%. Additionally, the Fed is due to publish its Beige Book. Traders see a 77% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 51% a month ago, while pricing in about 75 basis points of tightening by late 2027, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. Investors abandoned bets on a Fed rate hike later this month after two policymakers argued for gathering [USN:L6N45N16X TEXT:"more evidence before deciding"] whether further tightening is needed, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller said [USN:L1N45Z0AY TEXT:"inflation expectations remained "well anchored.""] Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin is scheduled to participate in a fireside chat in Virginia, while Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman is set to take part in talks in Bangkok. The International Monetary Fund and World Bank's annual meetings continue in Bangkok, with several appearances expected by European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde on Wednesday. The Australian dollar strengthened 0.06% versus the greenback to $0.6984, while New Zealand's kiwi strengthened 0.09% to $0.5614.

item.title: Singapore keeps monetary policy unchanged, surprising analysts
item.description: Singapore's central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged on Wednesday in a move that surprised analysts, with economic growth and inflation expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate.
item.dc:creator: Xinghui Kok, Jun Yong
item.content:encoded: Singapore's central bank kept its monetary settings unchanged on Wednesday in a move that surprised analysts, with economic growth and inflation expected to ease slightly as the AI boom and supply constraints moderate. All 10 analysts polled by Reuters had expected the Monetary Authority of Singapore to [USN:L6N45V03B TEXT:"tighten monetary policy"] as robust growth and inflation risks bolstered the case for another such move. "The Singapore economy should continue to expand at a firm pace in the immediate quarters ahead, and moderate thereafter as the AI cycle eases from its exceptional pace and global financial conditions tighten," the MAS said in a statement. "Core inflation is projected to ease discernibly from the middle of next year, as supply-driven imported inflation slows and domestic costs stay subdued." OCBC economist Selena Ling said she was surprised and that it must have been a close call for the central bank. "MAS's assessment of the core inflation trajectory is key - while remaining slightly elevated in the immediate quarters ahead, its expected to ease more discernibly from mid-2027 as supply-driven imported inflation slows and domestic costs stay subdued," said Ling. The central bank said it would maintain the prevailing rate of appreciation in its [USN:L6N45Z04Q TEXT:"exchange rate-based policy band"] known as the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate, or S$NEER. There would be no change to the width of the policy band or the level at which it is centred, it said. "The current appreciating policy band will allow the S$NEER to continue to strengthen and lean against the anticipated near-term rise in imported inflation, ensuring the gradual easing of inflationary pressures in 2027," the MAS said. The Singapore dollar held steady at 1.2802 per US dollar after MAS kept policy unchanged. SLIGHT MODERATION IN INFLATION The central bank [USN:P8N3LJ075 TEXT:"surprised"] markets in July by "very slightly" tightening policy, adding to a similar move in April this year. Preliminary government data earlier on Wednesday showed the economy [USN:P8N3Z500M TEXT:"grew"] 5.4% in the third quarter of 2026 from the same period last year. Core [USN:LUN3ZK00L TEXT:"inflation in August"] stood at 2.2%, official data showed last month. On Wednesday, MAS narrowed its core and headline inflation forecasts to 1.5%-2% and 2% respectively, from 1.5%-2.5%. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin said rising interest rates and a K-shaped labour market will help contain wage cost pressures and work in MAS’s favour. "Whether MAS tightens further remains open-ended and will depend on how energy prices and the AI-led boom evolves," Chua said. In August, the trade ministry [USN:L1N448001 TEXT:"upgraded"] its growth forecast for this year to 4.5% to 5.5%, from 2.0% to 4.0%, saying the impact of the Middle East war had been less severe than initially feared while the global AI investment boom had been stronger than expected. Instead of using interest rates, Singapore [USN:L6N45Z04Q TEXT:"manages monetary policy"] by letting the local dollar rise or fall against the currencies of its main trading partners within the undisclosed S$NEER trading band. It adjusts policy via three levers: the slope, mid-point and width of the policy band.

item.title: Trump says Taiwan agrees to buy 30% of LNG from Alaska pipeline project
item.description: Taiwan has agreed to buy 30% of the liquefied natural gas from a pipeline project in Alaska, US President Donald Trump told a rally in the state on Tuesday, but the deal terms were not immediately clear.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: Taiwan has agreed to buy 30% of the liquefied natural gas from a pipeline project in Alaska, US President Donald Trump told a rally in the state on Tuesday, but the deal terms were not immediately clear. Taiwan has committed to investing $4.4 billion in the development of the pipeline, said Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who also appeared at the rally organized by the Republican National Committee. Taiwan's economy ministry, which is in charge of energy policy, had no immediate comment. Asked about Trump's comments, Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai told reporters that the government's job is to "stabilize the entire energy supply and build its resilience, like governments everywhere." Trump's remarks come after Taiwan officials said in February they would [USN:P8N3V205D TEXT:"ramp up"] purchases of US natural gas to constitute about a third of the island's imported supply this year, and reduce purchases from other countries. Taiwan state energy firm CPC Corp signed an [USN:P8N3OD0AK TEXT:"agreement"] with Alaska Gasline Development Corp last year to buy LNG and invest in the pipeline project. Alaska's governor said last year that Taiwan [USN:L3N3QA0IH TEXT:"signed"] a letter of intent to buy 6 million metric tons of LNG per annum from the project. The investment would ensure Taiwan's energy security, President Lai Ching-te said at the time. Trump's comments did not make it clear whether a final deal had been signed. UP TO 20 MILLION TONS OF LNG EXPORTS A YEAR Last year, Taiwan Presidential Office Secretary-General Pan Men-an visited the site of the proposed LNG project in Alaska that the Trump administration has been pushing hard to allies in Asia as a supply option. If built, the [USN:L4N45M0CI TEXT:"Alaska LNG"] project will export up to 20 million tons of the superchilled gas a year. So far it has lined up agreements covering 13 million tons a year from buyers in Asia and French major TotalEnergies. It needs agreements for another 3 million tons and must turn them into binding deals in order to line up financing for the project. It would open direct access for US-made LNG to Asian markets including Taiwan without having to go through the Panama Canal or around the Horn of Africa, reducing transit time and costs. Taiwan has pledged to massively ramp up its purchases from the United States, including energy, to reduce a yawning trade surplus that has angered Washington. Trump said last month that South Korea had agreed to invest in the [USN:L1N45M0IK TEXT:"$54 billion pipeline"] for the Alaska LNG project, but Seoul said it was not yet set in stone.

item.title: Aluminium's calm belies lingering supply-chain stress
item.description: Iranian missile attacks on Gulf smelters and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz have knocked out almost 3 million metric tons of aluminium production capacity. Yet, eight months on, the market is seemingly unconcerned.
item.dc:creator: Andy Home
item.content:encoded: Iranian missile attacks on Gulf smelters and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz have knocked out almost 3 million metric tons of [USN:L8N43P15H TEXT:"aluminium production"] capacity. Yet, eight months on, the market is seemingly unconcerned. Indeed, London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month aluminium is now trading just above $3,000 per ton, which is where it was in early February before the US and Israel unleashed Operation Epic Fury against Iran. Traders are betting that a combination of rising output in Indonesia and higher product exports from China can tide things over until the Gulf smelters are repaired and shipping fully resumes in the Strait of Hormuz. The surface calm, however, masks lingering stress in a physical supply chain that is still reeling from the unprecedented disruption. PLUGGING THE GAPS Gulf production of primary aluminium slumped by an annualized 2.8 million tons between February and May, according to the International Aluminium Institute. The collapse reflected the forced shutdown of Emirates Global Aluminium's Al-Taweelah smelter and damage to Aluminium Bahrain's (ALBH.BH) facility, as well as logistics problems at other Gulf operators. Regional production has since been creeping higher as both plants [USN:L1N44907E TEXT:"undergo repairs"] and ramp production back up, but the August run-rate of 3.5 million tons annualised was still 2.6 million tons below pre-hostility levels. China and Indonesia have stepped in to plug the gap. China's exports of primary metal are constrained by a hefty 30% export duty, but outbound volumes of alloy doubled year-on-year to 349,000 tons in the January to August period. Exports of semi-finished products such as aluminium plate, sheet and strip surged by 774,000 tons to 4.46 million tons over the same period. Indonesia's [USN:L8N44Z0XJ TEXT:"new"] Chinese-owned smelters are also ramping up at speed. The country exported 114,000 tons of primary metal in July, a fresh monthly record. Around half of last year's Indonesian aluminium exports went to China but shipments since the Iran war have been dispersed across Asia, Europe and even the US. PHYSICAL STRESS Improved availability in Asia has caused physical premiums to ease from their June highs. Japanese buyers have negotiated a fourth-quarter delivery premium of $255 per ton over the LME cash price, which marks a 35% decline from the previous quarter. However, that's still higher than the $200-per-ton premium that was trading at the start of the Iran war, attesting to continued tension even in this relatively well-supplied part of the market. European buyers are paying significantly more for their physical metal. The CME European duty-paid premium is trading at $559 per ton over LME cash, double the level at the end of February. US buyers, of course, are paying more than anyone else for their aluminium with the US Midwest premium trading at an elevated $2,312 per ton over LME cash, though this is as much about President Donald Trump's 50% [USN:S0N3RL03L TEXT:"import tariffs"] as anything else. LOW INVENTORY Elevated premiums are sucking available metal into the physical supply chain, leaving LME stocks at multi-year lows. Registered inventory of 238,625 tons is the lowest level this century. Most of what remains is Russian metal, which reduces its appeal to most Western buyers. LME off-warrant inventory has also been steadily shrinking since February and now totals just 73,509 tons, which is the lowest reading since the LME introduced this category of stocks reporting in 2020. Time-spreads have eased considerably since June, when the cash premium over three-month metal jumped to over $100 per ton. But there is lingering tightness in the front part of the curve. After a period of mild contango, cash has just returned to a small premium over three-month metal again. Time-spread tension is likely to remain a feature of the London market as long as physical premiums remain so high. The aluminium market has proved highly resilient to the sudden loss of so much production, but the stress lines are still there beneath the calm surface.
